title: host_of() disagrees with the browser on backslash-userinfo URLs: resolve() releases the secret for 'https://evil.test\@pathlynks.test', which Chromium (WHATWG) navigates to evil.test
evidence: src/autotester/browser/secrets.py:60-63 host_of uses urllib.parse.urlparse, which treats 'evil.test\\' as userinfo and returns hostname 'pathlynks.test'. WHATWG URL (what Chromium/Playwright implement; verified with node `new URL(...)`): backslash is a path separator in special schemes, so host='evil.test', path='/@pathlynks.test'. Probe: SecretStore(proj(domains=['pathlynks.test']),{'PW':'supersecretvalue'}).resolve('{{SECRET:PW}}','https://evil.test\\@pathlynks.test') RETURNED the value. B3 says scoping is enforced against the current page host; here the page host would be evil.test. Note: 'https://evil.test%2F@pathlynks.test' is consistent on both parsers (host pathlynks.test) and is NOT a leak; the cycle-1 userinfo probe ('a.test@evil.test') was the safe direction. Fix direction (fail closed, two lines): in host_of() return '' when the raw input contains a backslash or when urlparse yields a username/password (any userinfo) Ã¢â‚¬â€ an empty host already raises SecretScopeError since AT-001. Add both as tests. T-010 must additionally pass the browser's own page.url (post-navigation) to resolve(), never the step's intended URL. CYCLE-3 RE-CHECK: host_of (secrets.py:73-88) returns '' on any backslash or any urlparse userinfo; resolve() raises SecretScopeError on ''. Cross-checked 35 destinations against node v24 `new URL(...).hostname`: every case where urlparse and WHATWG disagree in the leak direction ('evil.test\@pathlynks.test', 'pathlynks.test@evil.test', 'https:\\pathlynks.test', 'evil.test:@pathlynks.test', '@pathlynks.test', U+2044 userinfo) now returns '' (refused). Remaining disagreements ('pathlynks%2Etest', 'pathlynksÃ¯Â¼Å½test', trailing-space host) are all in the safe direction (refused while the browser would visit the legit host). Pinned by test_at007_backslash_and_userinfo_destinations_fail_closed.

title: Onboarding accepts an allowed_domains value that makes the project permanently unrunnable, and says nothing -- a project whose base_url host is not inside its own allowed_domains fails every run at execution time with a NavigationRefused the user cannot act on, and there is no UI to edit the value afterwards
evidence: Umesh onboarded the ERP project through the UI typing 'all' in Allowed domains, plainly meaning 'allow everything'. The form accepted it verbatim, so projects/erp/project.json holds allowed_domains: ['all'] while base_url is 'https://www.vidysea.com/erp'. The first real run (run-01M1WSZWBP57PNNR9N6DMJMHW6) came back INCONCLUSIVE, scoreboard 'not judged: execution errored', note "NavigationRefused: 'https://www.vidysea.com/erp' is outside allowed domains ['all']" -- i.e. the project could never have tested anything from the moment it was created. Two distinct defects: (1) ui/app.py::onboard_submit does no validation that the project's OWN base_url host falls inside the allowed_domains it is being given, so an obviously self-contradictory project is persisted silently; (2) there is no route anywhere to edit a project's allowed_domains/base_url after onboarding, so a user who gets it wrong once cannot fix it from the UI at all (ui/routes_credentials.py edits .env values only, never project.json). NOT fixed by widening allowed_domains to support a literal 'all'/wildcard: allowed_domains is a documented hard security boundary ('the browser will never navigate outside these', CLAUDE.md + ARCHITECTURE.md security section), and adding an allow-anything escape hatch is a security-model change requiring an explicit decision, not a bug fix. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): _require_reachable_base_url exists in src/autotester/ui/helpers.py and guards the onboarding path.
found_by: umesh+maker (live end-to-end run of the new add-a-case flow)
checker_note: Both halves verified by /checker unit ui-project-edit-and-domain-validation cycle 1. (1) Prevention: POST /onboard with base_url=https://www.vidysea.com/erp + allowed_domains=all returns HTTP 400 naming 'www.vidysea.com' and creates no projects/erp-probe/ directory (re-run live against localhost:8010, not the maker's paste). (2) Recovery: seeded a scratch project in the exact broken state (allowed_domains ['all']), reached GET /projects/chk-broken/edit (200), fixed it via POST (303), and confirmed browser.session.check_destination(project, base_url) then returns 'www.vidysea.com' instead of raising NavigationRefused -- the recovered project passes the REAL navigation gate, not just the validator. Validator proven equal to the boundary: session.check_destination is host_of + Project.allows_domain and _require_reachable_base_url composes the identical pair, so no over-tightening; all four on-disk projects (pathlynks, vidysea-erp, regression-demo, erp) still pass. The wildcard half stays deliberately unfixed and is NOT a residue of this issue: expressing 'allow everything' is a security-boundary widening reserved to Umesh, and the user's actual intent is fully expressible because the error names the exact host to add.

title: A case's auto-generated default rubric is persisted keyed on the case id, but its criterion text derives from case.rationale which is NOT part of that id -- so changing a case's rationale silently keeps grading against the OLD claim forever, with no invalidation path
evidence: Found live while proving the new UI add-a-case flow end to end. stages/run_case_pipeline.py::default_rubric builds its single criterion as f'The evidence is consistent with: {case.rationale or ...}' and the result is saved to projects/<slug>/rubrics/rub_<case_id>.json. Case.compute_id() (schema/case.py) hashes only (project, flow_id, case_class, steps) -- rationale is deliberately excluded, so two cases differing only in rationale are the SAME case id by design. Consequence observed: a case created with rationale 'added by hand from the UI' persisted a rubric whose claim was literally 'The evidence is consistent with: added by hand from the UI'; after the rationale was corrected to None and the case re-created through the real HTTP form (same id, correctly deduped), run-01M1WT69EQFRYZC4NYHEY0FY1Z STILL graded against the stale rubric and FAILed with 'Evidence shows only login page; manual addition not performed' -- a hallucinated criterion, on a screenshot that plainly showed the sign-in page the case actually asked for. Deleting projects/erp/rubrics/rub_case_27256e2a2b8d.json was the only way to recover. The bug is the missing invalidation, not the dedup: either the rubric file should be content-addressed on the claim text it was built from, or load_rubric should regenerate when the stored claim no longer matches the case's current rationale/title. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): Provenance stamping is present in stages/run_case_pipeline.py.
found_by: umesh+maker (live end-to-end run of the new add-a-case flow)

title: _require_reachable_base_url's 'browser can open it' half is much weaker than it reads -- host_of returns a non-empty pseudo-host for arbitrary garbage, so a base_url with no scheme (or literally 'all') still onboards a project no browser can open
evidence: Found by /checker while probing unit ui-project-edit-and-domain-validation live. src/autotester/ui/helpers.py:53-55 refuses only when host_of() returns EMPTY, and browser/secrets.py:70-84 returns empty only for a backslash, userinfo, or an unparseable authority -- urlparse('//all').hostname is 'all'. title: Onboarding and the new edit form disagree on whitespace: edit strips name/base_url before saving, onboarding stores them verbatim, so the same value entered in the two places produces two different project.json files
evidence: Found by /checker while probing unit ui-project-edit-and-domain-validation live. ui/routes_project_edit.py:72-74 saves name.strip() and base_url.strip(); ui/app.py::onboard_submit passes name and base_url straight into Project(...) with no strip (only allowed_domains is split-and-stripped in both). title: is_stale_default compares only criteria and no_fire, so a human edit confined to a rubric's feedback_format is silently discarded when the rubric is regenerated for a stale claim
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit grade-stale-rubric-invalidation. src/autotester/stages/run_case_pipeline.py:83 returns `rubric.criteria == untouched.criteria and rubric.no_fire == untouched.no_fire` -- Rubric.feedback_format (schema/verdict.py:36, consumed by stages/grade.py:47 as {{FORMAT}}) is not part of the comparison. Not a FAIL of this unit: no contract criterion covers feedback_format, regeneration is the desired behaviour in that scenario (the claim really was stale), and no code path anywhere sets feedback_format -- grep finds only the schema default and grade.py's read -- so the field is reachable only by hand-editing JSON. Fix direction if queued: include feedback_format in the untouched-comparison, or document it as deliberately excluded because it is presentation, not the grading claim.

title: A generator-stamped rubric shared by two cases via case.rubric_ref would be rewritten with the pointing case's claim, destroying the other case's grading contract
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit grade-stale-rubric-invalidation. run_case_pipeline.py:96 resolves `rubric_id = case.rubric_ref or f'rub_{case.id}'`, and is_stale_default (line 82) rebuilds the untouched shape with `rubric.case_id or case.id` -- it never checks that rubric.case_id actually IS this case. Reproduced in-container: a rubric carrying GENERATOR provenance whose case_id is 'some_other_case_id' returns is_stale_default == True against an unrelated case, so run_and_grade_case would save that case's claim over it. title: The 4 pre-existing unstamped rubrics on disk are NOT in fact indistinguishable from hand-written ones -- they carry the generator's exact template -- but they can never self-heal, so AT-059's failure mode stays latent for those cases
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit grade-stale-rubric-invalidation. The manifest's stated limitation says rubrics written before provenance stamping are 'genuinely indistinguishable from hand-written ones'. Checker-verified against all 5 rubric files in the 4 real projects: projects/pathlynks/rubrics/{rub_case_35b17ccece2d,rub_case_a5ea57c0961a,rub_case_b1cb019ebb56}.json and projects/vidysea-erp/rubrics/rub_case_7ba94f4da443.json all have provenance null AND carry _rubric_for_claim's exact output -- a single criterion id 'c1' with the text "The evidence is consistent with: <claim>. If you cite this as a failure, use criterion id 'c1' exactly - do not invent a different id." and no_fire == ['exact wording of any error message shown by the product']. Every hand-written rubric in the repo differs in shape (scripts/run_pathlynks_first_cases.py:91 uses criterion id 'landed'; scripts/regression_proof.py:93 and scripts/bench_trial.py:83 use no_fire ['visual styling'] and different wording), so shape alone does distinguish them. Currently harmless -- checker re-derived claim_of(case) for all 5 and none is stale today, and none would be rewritten by the next run. Not a FAIL: refusing to touch an unstamped rubric is the safe direction, and a template-shape heuristic would reintroduce exactly the overwrite-on-a-guess risk the unit exists to avoid. Fix direction if queued: a one-off migration that stamps provenance on rubrics whose shape is byte-identical to _rubric_for_claim(embedded_claim, ...), reviewed by a human per file -- not an automatic runtime heuristic.

title: test_deleting_then_re_adding_the_same_steps_works cannot exercise the _case_ids cache it is documented as proving -- every UI request builds a fresh ProjectStore, so the test would pass unchanged even if delete_case never discarded the id
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-case-management. tests/test_ui_case_management.py:166-181 asserts that a delete followed by a re-add of identical steps succeeds, and both the test docstring and qa/manifests/ui-case-management.md claim this 'proves delete_case genuinely clears the id cache rather than leaving the duplicate guard to refuse a legitimate re-add'. It does not: src/autotester/ui/helpers.py:73 constructs `store = ProjectStore(slug)` per request, so ProjectStore._case_ids is None at the start of every HTTP call and is repopulated from disk by has_case/add_case. Deleting the `self._case_ids.discard(case_id)` line in project_store.py:116 would leave the test green. The checker verified the actual cache behaviour separately, in-container, within ONE store instance: add -> has_case True; delete_case -> True and has_case False; re-add of the identical (same-id) case in that same instance -> the row comes back (list_cases == ['B']); update_case keeps the id in the cache. So the CODE is correct -- only the test's proof-value claim is overstated. Not a FAIL of any ui.md criterion (none governs test coverage). Fix direction if queued: assert directly against one ProjectStore instance (add/delete/has_case/add), or drop the claim from the docstring and manifest. | FIXED 2026-09-07: added three store-level tests in tests/test_store.py that exercise the id cache against ONE ProjectStore instance, where it is actually observable: delete clears it (has_case False, and the re-add a stale cache would swallow succeeds), delete of an unknown id returns False, and update_case keeps the id cached while replacing in place rather than appending twice. Proof-value verified by sabotage, not assumed: replacing `self._case_ids.discard(case_id)` with a dead branch makes test_delete_case_clears_the_id_cache_within_one_store_instance FAIL, while the UI-level test AT-066 was filed against still passes -- which is precisely the gap the checker identified. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): Store-level id-cache tests are present in tests/test_store.py and the suite passes.

title: cases.jsonl whole-file rewrite (delete_case/update_case) can silently drop a row appended concurrently by a CLI script's add_case -- pre-existing with upsert_jsonl, now reachable from a UI button
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-case-management. store/filestore.py:75-88 (delete_jsonl_row) and :91-110 (upsert_jsonl) both read the whole file, filter/replace in memory, and _atomic_write the result -- a read-modify-write with no lock. Any row appended between the read and the os.replace is lost. Repo-wide the only writers to projects/<slug>/cases.jsonl are ProjectStore.add_case (append_jsonl), update_case and delete_case; grep over src and scripts finds add_case call sites at ui/routes_cases.py:188, scripts/bench_trial.py:118, scripts/regression_proof.py:147 and scripts/run_pathlynks_first_cases.py:161. There is no in-process concurrency (helpers.py:73 builds a fresh ProjectStore per request and nothing runs in the background), so the only real window is a human running one of those CLI scripts while clicking Rename/Delete in the UI. The write itself IS atomic -- checker-verified that a crash cannot truncate the file: mkstemp in the target's own directory, write, os.replace, unlink on any BaseException, and no orphan .tmp-* left on the success path. Both docstrings already state the caveat ('for a small collection a human curates, never for append-only history'). Not a FAIL: the unit introduces no new concurrency and no criterion covers it. Fix direction if queued: an advisory lock file per project directory around the read-modify-write, or make delete/update go through a single serialised writer.

title: The declare-secret 400 echoes the raw submitted key back to the caller -- and the form's own hint says the most likely wrong entry there is the credential VALUE itself
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-secrets-declaration. src/autotester/ui/routes_project_edit.py:176 raises `HTTPException(400, f"cannot declare '{key.strip()}': {why}")`. Reproduced live in-container: `POST /projects/erp/secrets key=hunter2` returns `{"detail":"cannot declare 'hunter2': String should match pattern '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$'"}` with content-type application/json. The card's own hint text (_secrets_card, line 75-76) reads 'CAPITALS, digits and underscores -- a name, never the value itself', which names pasting the value into the Key field as the anticipated user error; when that happens the value is reflected verbatim in the response body. NOT an XSS (the body is JSON, not HTML -- verified via content-type) and nothing is persisted (erp's secrets were unchanged after the probe), so no U3/U5 criterion is violated and this is not a FAIL. The exposure is bounded to the submitter's own response on a localhost single-operator tool, but it is the one place in this unit where a would-be credential is repeated back rather than dropped, and the project's stated discipline is that values are never echoed (routes_credentials.py never echoes the posted value). Fix direction if queued: drop the key from the message ('that is not a valid credential name: <reason>'), or echo only a length/shape summary. | FIXED 2026-09-07: the 400 no longer quotes the submitted key -- it reads 'cannot declare this credential: <pydantic msg>'. The form hint was also reworded to stop naming the value as a thing that could go in that box; it now says the box wants a NAME and that the value is entered later on the Credentials page. Regression test test_a_rejected_key_is_never_echoed_back asserts a password-shaped key is refused and its text absent from the response. | CHECKER-SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (re-run, not read): test_a_rejected_key_is_never_echoed_back present in the test suite and passing.

title: The paste-a-real-credential guard is applied to step_value ONLY -- the same credential typed into the case title, step_target or step_expected is accepted and written in cleartext to projects/<slug>/cases.jsonl, which IS git-tracked in a public repo
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. src/autotester/ui/routes_cases.py:116 calls `_refuse_unsafe_value(value.strip(), project, secrets)` inside _build_steps and nowhere else; `title` (routes_cases.py:154-157, checked only for non-blank), `target` (:121) and `expect` (:117-120) reach `Step`/`Case` unchecked. Reproduced in-container against a scratch AUTOTESTER_ROOT with a declared DEMO_PASSWORD whose .env value was 'hunter2-this-is-the-real-one': step_value=<value> -> 400 refused (correct); the identical value in step_target -> 303 and on disk as {"target":"hunter2-this-is-the-real-one"}; in step_expected -> 303 and on disk as {"expected":{"visible_text":["hunter2-this-is-the-real-one"]}}; in the title -> 303 and on disk as the case title. The manifest's own stated reason for the guard ('cases.jsonl is not gitignored') applies verbatim to all three: `git check-ignore .env` -> ignored by **/.env, but `git ls-files projects/pathlynks/cases.jsonl` returns the path, so that file is tracked and this repo is public (github.com/umeshsugara-ai/autoTesting). The three boxes sit on the SAME form row as the guarded one, so this is a plausible mis-field, not an attack. The title case is worse than a storage leak: `stages/run_case_pipeline.claim_of` returns `f"the case '{case.title}' completes as its steps describe"` when rationale is None (which U6 mandates), so the raw value reaches build_grade_prompt -- where the newly-wired `SecretStore.guard_prompt` then raises an UNHANDLED ValueError, turning every subsequent run into a 500 rather than a graded verdict (verified: REAL in claim_of(case) -> True; grade(..., secrets=store) on a payload carrying the value -> ValueError 'refusing to proceed: raw secret value present in payload'). Not a FAIL of any ui.md criterion -- none governs credential safety in cases; the maker correctly filed nothing and this row is the tracker. Fix direction: move the guard from _build_steps' value branch to every user-supplied string create_case persists (title, target, expected text), keeping the placeholder-vs-literal split as it is.

title: The raw-value guard is per-step-row, so a credential split across two rows passes and reassembles exactly -- the control is defence-in-depth, not a boundary, and the manifest presents it as protection
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. `Redactor.is_clean` (core/redact.py:52-54) tests `value in text` for each whole known .env value, and `_refuse_unsafe_value` is called once per surviving step row (routes_cases.py:116), so no cross-row or cross-field view of the submission exists. Reproduced in-container on a scratch root whose .env held only DEMO_PASSWORD=hunter2-this-is-the-real-one: a two-row submission with step_value[0]='hunter2-this-i' and step_value[1]='s-the-real-one' -> 303, both halves persisted to cases.jsonl, and half0+half1 == the real value byte for byte. Note this probe had to be re-run: a first attempt appeared to be caught, but only because the scratch .env also carried SHORT=a and the second half contains an 'a' -- the checker does not report a pass it cannot reproduce cleanly. Correctly CAUGHT in the same harness: the exact value; the value with surrounding whitespace (_build_steps strips before the guard, confirmed order at routes_cases.py:116); the value as a substring of a longer string ('prefix-<value>-suffix'); and an UNDECLARED .env value belonging to another project, because SecretStore.redactor() is built from _all_values() = shadow + declared (browser/secrets.py:_all_values). Severity medium not high: this needs deliberate action, unlike AT-070's adjacent-box slip. Fix direction: none required as a code change -- but the manifest/docs should say what this control is (a mistake-catcher over exact known values), so nobody later mistakes it for a boundary.

title: is_clean has no minimum length by design (AT-002), so a short or word-like .env value makes ordinary step text be refused with a message that wrongly tells the user they pasted a credential
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. core/redact.py:20-24 documents the absence of a minimum length as deliberate ('a three-character password is a bad password, but leaking it is still a leak'), and the checker agrees the direction is right -- it fails CLOSED. The cost is the message, not the refusal. Reproduced in-container with a scratch .env holding DEMO_TOKEN=test: step_value 'test' -> 400, 'latest news' -> 400, 'contest entry' -> 400, 'Bengaluru' -> 303. The refusal text is 'that looks like a real credential. Do not paste the value into a test step...', which is simply false for 'latest news' and gives the user no way to understand or proceed. title: Credential-entry round-trip is lossy and silent: a value saved through POST /projects/{slug}/env or POST /settings/providers is written verbatim by env_editor.set_env_value but read back through secrets.parse_env/_clean_value, which strips a whitespace-preceded '#' comment, strips leading/trailing whitespace, and unquotes a value beginning with a quote. A real password containing ' #', a leading or trailing space, or a leading quote is therefore silently stored as a DIFFERENT value while the page still shows '(dot) Set'.
evidence: checker probe in-container against a temp .env using the production functions: set_env_value + parse_env round-trip -> 'pa ss #word'->'pa ss' MANGLED, 'p@ss #1'->'p@ss' MANGLED, 'end '->'end' MANGLED, '"quoted"pw'->'quoted' MANGLED; 'pa ss#word' (no space before #), 'tab<TAB>pw', 'pw#nohash' and 'plain8chars' all round-trip OK; a value containing a newline is correctly refused (InvalidEnvValue). Pre-existing (env_editor.py + secrets._clean_value, untouched by this unit) but filed now because this is the exact route the operator is about to type a real ERP password into, and the failure mode is a run that cannot log in with no indication the stored value differs from what was typed. Fix direction: refuse (or quote-escape) a value that would not survive parse_env, or assert the round-trip after writing. | FIXED 2026-09-07 (cycle 2), verified by checker: env_editor._render_value() quotes with a character absent from the value and re-parses to prove the round-trip before writing. Checker re-probe, 17 values through set_env_value+parse_env on a temp .env (the 6 from the manifest plus whitespace-only, empty, trailing backslash, leading '#', bare '#', 'a=b=c', 4000 chars, unicode, 'export FOO=bar', unmatched leading quote, 'url#frag'): ALL round-trip exactly, zero mangled. A value with BOTH quote characters is REFUSED (InvalidEnvValue) and the target file is byte-identical after the refusal -- nothing half-written, because _render_value raises before env_path is read or opened. A realistic 6-line pre-existing .env (comment, blank, quoted-with-#, plain, `export `-prefixed, padded-quoted) survived all 17 writes with every prior key unchanged; newline injection still refused. Re-verified through the LIVE route POST /projects/{slug}/env for 8 values incl. "p@ss #1", '  spaced  ', "'quoted'" and 300 chars -- all exact, both-quotes -> 400, all pre-existing .env keys intact.

title: U8 REGRESSION introduced by ui-credential-guard-project-routes cycle 2: the AT-078 fix narrowed the input guard from 'every value in .env' to 'values some project has DECLARED as a SecretRef', so an UNDECLARED real credential in .env is no longer refused and is written in cleartext to git-tracked cases.jsonl and project.json. Criterion U8 says a raw .env value in any of those fields is refused (400); it is not.
evidence: checker cycle-2 probe, live at http://localhost:8000 in-container after `docker compose restart autotester`, using the operator's REAL GEMINI_API_KEY (39 chars, a live model-provider key present in .env and undeclared by all four projects, whose declared keys are only ERP_EMAIL/ERP_PASSWORD/PATHLYNKS_COUNSELLOR_EMAIL/PASSWORD/PATHLYNKS_USER_EMAIL/PASSWORD). On a throwaway project: POST /projects/<scratch>/cases with title=<GEMINI_API_KEY> -> 200, and the key was then read back verbatim out of projects/<scratch>/cases.jsonl (`GK in cases.jsonl == True`); same with step_value=<GEMINI_API_KEY> -> 200. POST /projects/vidysea-erp/edit with name=<GEMINI_API_KEY> -> 200 and the key was confirmed on disk in projects/vidysea-erp/project.json (restored immediately with `git checkout --`); POST /projects/<x>/secrets with description=<GEMINI_API_KEY> -> 200. In-process probe of helpers._refuse_unsafe_value over EVERY .env key confirms the split: PATHLYNKS_*_EMAIL/PASSWORD (declared) REFUSED, while PATHLYNKS_MONGO_URI, GEMINI_API_KEY, and both LOGIN_URLs are ALLOWED. Cycle 1 refused all of these. Fix direction: do NOT trade scope for editability -- restore the full-.env scope for the input guard and fix AT-078 the narrow way instead, by exempting only text byte-identical to the value ALREADY persisted for that same field of that same project (a no-op re-save cannot be a new leak, since the value is already on disk), or by an explicit non-secret config allowlist. title: deny_reason.never-click is bypassable through SafetyPolicy construction, contradicting the manifest's claim that "there is no policy setting that makes the explorer click a logout control; it would need a code change" -- policy_for(project, never_click_patterns=[]) (or SafetyPolicy(write_policy=ALLOW_WRITES, never_click_patterns=[]) directly) produces a SafetyPolicy under which deny_reason(logout_el, pol) returns None, i.e. a logout control is allowed through. never_click_patterns is an ordinary overridable SafetyPolicy field with no floor enforced anywhere (no min-length validator, no hardcoded fallback), so the same policy_for(**overrides) escape hatch documented for legitimate deny_patterns localization also silently disarms the one guard D-016 says configuration must never be able to loosen. Not exploitable today (no caller exists yet -- T-143 is unbuilt), so this does not fail core-invariants C1-C3, but it should be closed before T-143 wires a real crawl loop through this policy, e.g. by hardcoding the never-click regex independent of any policy field, or by giving SafetyPolicy a validator that refuses an empty never_click_patterns.

title: DEFAULT_NEVER_CLICK_PATTERNS misses hyphen/underscore/dot-separated logout control names -- "Log-Out", "Sign-Out", "LOG_OUT", and "Log.Out" all return None from deny_reason (not denied), because both never-click patterns use [\s\w]{0,10} or a literal " ?" between the two words, and neither \s nor \w matches a hyphen, underscore, or dot. This is a coverage gap in the never-click baseline itself (schema/crawl.py DEFAULT_NEVER_CLICK_PATTERNS), not a policy-construction bypass -- AT-092's fix (checking the baseline unconditionally) is unaffected and still correctly denies every space/adjacent-word variant it targets. No false positives introduced or found: 'checkout', 'workout tracker', 'about us', 'output settings', 'Log in to your account' all correctly stay un-denied under the same probe. Not exploitable today (T-143's crawler does not exist yet), but real product UIs commonly render 'Log-Out' or 'LOG_OUT' as a button's accessible name (design-system kebab-case or CSS text-transform on a snake_case id), so this should be closed before T-143 wires a real crawl loop through this guard.
evidence: checker adversarial probe inside docker compose exec autotester, python one-liner against src/autotester/stages/explore_safety.py::deny_reason and schema/crawl.py::DEFAULT_NEVER_CLICK_PATTERNS (r"\blog ?out\b", r"\blog\b[\s\w]{0,10}\bout\b", r"\bsign ?out\b", r"\bsignout\b", r"\bsign\b[\s\w]{0,10}\bout\b"): deny_reason(ElementRef(role='button', name='Log-Out', ...), policy_for(project)) -> None; same for 'Sign-Out', 'LOG_OUT', 'Log.Out'. Fix direction: widen the character class to allow a bounded run of separator punctuation (e.g. [\s\w.-]{0,3} between 'log'/'sign' and 'out' for the adjacent-word pattern) alongside the existing word-gap pattern, with a new parametrised test pinning both the separator variants and the existing no-false-positive set. title: store/filestore.py::append_jsonl documents itself as "cheap and crash-safe (a torn write can only ever damage the last line, never an earlier one)", but read_jsonl RAISES ValueError on any malformed row rather than skipping it -- so a torn final line does not merely damage that line, it makes the ENTIRE file unloadable. This narrows the explore.md X11 partial-graph guarantee more than the docstring implies: a crawl killed BETWEEN writes leaves a fully loadable graph (checker proved this live), but a crawl killed DURING a single node/edge/issue append leaves nodes.jsonl unreadable and the partial graph lost. Affects every JSONL artifact in the system (cases, results, issues), not just crawls -- the crawl stage is simply the first writer that runs long enough for a mid-append kill to be realistic. Not a defect introduced by this unit; the honest scope is now recorded in qa/contracts/explore.md X11. Fix options: have read_jsonl tolerate a malformed FINAL line (skip with a warning) while still raising on a malformed interior line, or write each row with a single atomic os.write of a pre-encoded buffer.
evidence: src/autotester/store/filestore.py:67-72 append_jsonl (docstring claims crash-safe) vs :52-64 read_jsonl ("A malformed row raises with its line number" -- raises ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: {exc}")). The mid-append case was NOT induced and is not claimed to be safe.

title: stages/explore.py::_seed swallows the seed exception entirely (except Exception: return None), so a crawl that cannot start reports the single generic stop_reason "could not open base_url" with the cause discarded -- a NavigationRefused (the X7 security refusal) is indistinguishable from a DNS failure, a timeout or a TLS error.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore.py:93-98 `_seed`: try { goto(base_url); settle(); observe() } except Exception: return None -- the exception object is never bound, logged, or attached to the crawl. Caller at :179-181: `if _seed(rt) is None: rt.stop_reason = "could not open base_url"; return _finish(rt, CrawlStatus.ABORTED)`. Detection is NOT lost (the crawl does abort and does say so), but the diagnosis is: every distinct failure mode collapses to one string. This bites T-145 directly (the live logged-in ERP crawl), where an operator seeing "could not open base_url" cannot tell whether the ERP was down or whether the crawl was refused by its own domain guard. Related and lower: `_recover` at explore_node.py:145-150 is `except Exception: pass`, so a failed recovery is unrecorded -- though the caller returns False regardless, so the node status is still written. Fix direction: bind the exception and set stop_reason to f"could not open base_url: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", and record NavigationRefused distinctly from a transport error. Not a contract-sanctioned fallback: qa/contracts/explore.md does not ask for the cause to be dropped -- contrast explore_node.capture, whose "never fatal" swallow IS documented B7 behaviour and is deliberately NOT flagged here.

title: The (correct) same-crawl SPA exemption in merge_screens is scoped to ONE CRAWL, not to one SOURCE: a second SPA state discovered by a LATER crawl at a url_pattern an earlier crawl already merged does file a Conflict, even though both claims come from the crawler and neither disagrees with the other.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore_merge.py:99-100 `by_pattern = {s.url_pattern: s for s in spec.screens if s.url_pattern}` is built from the PRE-EXISTING spec only, and screens added during this merge are put into `known_ids` but never into `by_pattern` -- which is exactly what makes the intra-crawl exemption work. Probed live 2026-09-08: the identical SPA pair (same '/' pattern, signatures sig_plain / sig_filters, names 'Home' and 'Home with filters open') gives screens=2 conflicts=0 when merged in one call, and screens=2 conflicts=1 when merged as crawl c1 then crawl c2 -- claims ["existing screen 'Home' (node_4c6a215b75e5)", "crawled screen 'Home with filters open' (node_16734fb626aa)"]. Consequence: a project that re-crawls (the intended workflow -- the UI has an 'Explore again' button) accumulates false Conflicts on every SPA whose states are found across separate crawls. Fails safe (both screens are kept, nothing is overwritten), so it is noise for the human reviewer rather than data loss. Fix direction: exempt a clash whose existing screen's source_ref.source_id is itself a crawl id, i.e. scope the exemption to 'the crawler as a source' rather than 'this crawl run'.

title: explore_node.return_to() discards the cause of a failed return -- the same shape AT-098 just fixed at _seed, one level down. A NavigationRefused (the X7 SECURITY refusal) hit while getting back onto a node is indistinguishable from a timeout or a torn page, and the first call site records no reason at all.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore_node.py:135-138 `except Exception: _recover(rt); return False` -- the exception is never bound. Two call sites in visit_node: :182 `if not return_to(...): _mark(rt, node, NodeStatus.ABORTED_ERROR); return` records the node status with NO reason string anywhere, and :198 records an edge with the fixed literal 'could not return to this screen'. So a crawl that stops exploring a node because the browser was refused off-domain on the way back reads exactly like one that hit a slow page. AT-098's own evidence flagged this as 'related and lower' (_recover at explore_node.py:145-150 is `except Exception: pass`); AT-098 is closed on its stated scope (_seed), so the residual is filed here rather than lost. Not a criterion violation: no X-criterion requires a return_to reason, and it fails safe -- the node is marked and the crawl continues. Fix direction: bind the exception in return_to, return the reason, and pass it into _mark / record_edge the way try_action already does at :103-107. Deliberately NOT flagged: explore_node.py:33 (capture's 'never fatal' swallow, documented B7 behaviour) and _recover's own inner `except Exception: pass` (last-ditch recovery, the caller already returns False).

title: The AT-103 fix widened the SPA exemption from 'one crawl' to 'both claims are structural', which also makes a GENUINE product change unreportable: a later crawl finding a structurally different screen at a url_pattern an earlier crawl already claimed is now silently two screens and never a Conflict, and the stale screen is kept forever with nothing marking it stale.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore_merge.py:110 `if clash is None or clash.name == incoming.name or _is_structural(clash): return None`. Probed live 2026-09-08 (checker script, container): crawl c1 finds /settings (sig_v1, 'Settings'); the product ships a redesign; crawl c2 finds /settings (sig_v2, 'Account settings') and v1 no longer exists -> screens=2 conflicts=0, both rows kept ('node_1adc40552' src=c1, 'node_bc8e052c9' src=c2), review note '1 screen(s) added by crawl c2 -- needs review' -- byte-identical to what an innocent SPA re-crawl says, so the human cannot tell the two apart. Two crawls at different times ARE two sources with distinct source_ids and their claims genuinely differ; pre-fix (a195fbf) this filed a Conflict. NOT a violation of X14 as written (its own AT-103 residual paragraph prescribed this widening) and it fails safe -- both screens survive, nothing is overwritten, the version bumps and Review resets to DRAFT -- so it is a residual, not a regression to revert. Note also that a Conflict was always a poor instrument here: it caught a product change only when the URL was kept AND the name changed, and never caught a screen that vanished or moved. Fix direction: do NOT re-narrow _is_structural (that reinstates a false conflict on every SPA state on every re-crawl, which is the intended workflow -- the UI has an 'Explore again' button). Add the missing mechanism instead: last-seen/staleness on Screen (a screen not observed by the latest crawl of this project), surfaced on the crawl page and the workbook, which reports disappearance and redesign alike.

title: The RunApproval tamper check is defeated by recomputing the id: content_id is an UNKEYED sha256, so anyone who can write approvals.jsonl -- including the autonomous crawler the gate exists to bound -- can widen a grant and mint a matching id. Caught a careless edit, did not stop a forger.
evidence: Proven end to end on disk in the running container, scratch AUTOTESTER_ROOT=/tmp/advroot2. Baseline: a human grant of max_actions=12 via `uv run autotester approve` -> appr_f3616d0cafd7. (a) Editing max_actions to 9999 while keeping the stored id IS caught: `check_crawl_approval.py demo` and a real `autotester explore` both refuse with 'appr_f3616d0cafd7: edited after it was granted (content id no longer matches)'. (b) Rewriting the same row with max_actions=9999, wall_clock_s=99999.0, production=True and the `id` key REMOVED -> schema/approval.py model_post_init mints the matching id (id has default ""), forged row appr_34d709b1d3ea, is_intact=True. Pasting a self-computed id is identical. `AUTOTESTER_ROOT=/tmp/advroot2 uv run autotester explore demo --max-actions 500 --wall-clock 300` then RAN: crawl_01M1ZD9VR9SKRN9B748KKH721V completed -- a 500-action production-flagged crawl on a human grant of 12. Root cause: core/ids.py content_id() is a plain sha256 with no secret, so the mapping is public. NOT charged as a failure -- CN3 as filed claims only id-mismatch detection, which is exactly true, and no unkeyed local scheme can do better. HUMAN_GATE for Umesh (do not let the maker pick): HMAC keyed from the repo-root .env (already the credential boundary and gitignored), a separate signed/append-only audit line, or is 'accident detection only' the accepted posture? Independently of that decision, the operator-facing prose overclaims and must be corrected: schema/approval.py module docstring ('an approval cannot be edited on disk to widen itself') and cli_crawl.approve_cmd's docstring, which is `--help` text an operator reads ('editing the row afterwards to widen it invalidates it'). Recorded as a stated limitation in qa/contracts/consent.md CN3.

evidence: Measured live in the container against fb261c5. title: The Files-API upload cache is keyed on `resolve()::st_size`, so a recording edited or re-exported in place at the same byte size is a cache HIT and the pipeline reads the OLD video while reporting the new one -- and this unit already computes a sha256 of the same file two modules away.
evidence: gemini_files.py:61 `key = f"{path.resolve()}::{path.stat().st_size if path.exists() else 0}"`. Reproduced by the checker at 1c8c8e4 with a stub client: upload v.mp4 (100 bytes) -> cached; rewrite the SAME path with 100 DIFFERENT bytes; call `upload_and_wait` again -> `files.upload` call count 0, the cached handle for the old content is returned. Neither content nor mtime is in the key. Every other cache-degradation path probed is CORRECT and is now required by contract I9 -- a dead handle raises inside the try and re-uploads (upload count 1), a cached handle still PROCESSING re-uploads, an expired entry (TTL 46h) misses, and a corrupt cache file (`{not json`) is swallowed by _load_cache's ValueError branch and rewritten cleanly -- so this is the one key that fails toward a plausible wrong answer instead of toward a re-upload. Probability is low (an edit landing on an identical byte count) but the consequence is a FlowSpec provenance-stamped to a recording the model never watched. Fix direction: key on `file_sha256(path)` -- `core.ids.file_sha256` is already imported by stages/ingest.py for `register_source`, so the digest for this exact file is computed anyway -- or at minimum add `st_mtime_ns`.

title: `Source.sha256` is recorded at registration and never re-checked at ingest time, so `ingest_video` will watch a file whose bytes no longer match the Source describing it and stamp every SourceRef with the wrong recording's identity.
evidence: Executed by the checker at 1c8c8e4: `register_source(store, c)` with content b'v1' mints src_A carrying sha256(v1); rewriting c.mp4 to b'v2-different' and calling `register_source` again correctly mints a NEW src_B -- provenance rows are immutable, which is the right call -- but the OLD row src_A survives on disk still pointing at c.mp4 with a sha that no longer describes it. `ingest_video` (stages/ingest.py:129-145) opens `Path(source.path)` and never compares `file_sha256(path)` against `source.sha256`; `cli_video.run_cmd` selects a source by id and does not either. So `autotester ingest run demo src_A` silently watches v2 and writes a FlowSpec whose every Screen and Step SourceRef points into a video that no longer exists at those timestamps -- and I2's whole promise (a human can jump to the second the system learned a step) quietly stops being true. Nothing warns. Fix direction: verify the digest in `ingest_video` (or in `run_cmd`) and raise naming both hashes; a stale Source should be re-registered, not silently re-watched.

title: `google-genai` is imported directly by `providers/gemini.py` and `gemini_files.py` but is not declared in `pyproject.toml` (plan section 4 A2 assigns the declaration to T-131); it resolves today only as a transitive dependency of `langchain-google-genai`.
evidence: Ruled on by the checker at the maker's explicit request. `from google import genai` (gemini.py:106) and `from google.genai import types` (gemini.py:65) are direct imports; `pyproject.toml` dependencies list `langchain-google-genai>=4.4.0` and no `google-genai`. But uv.lock shows exactly one package requiring it -- langchain-google-genai 4.4.0 lists `{ name = "google-genai" }` -- so GeminiProvider is importable by the accident of another library's pin, and a langchain-google-genai release that drops or renames that dependency breaks the vision provider with no pyproject change and no failing test (no test imports google.genai; the 29 tests in test_providers.py + test_ingest.py + test_ingest_persist.py all pass with socket.connect and socket.getaddrinfo blocked). Fix direction: add `google-genai>=2.22.0` to `[project].dependencies` in the A3 unit that first calls the Files API for real, per the ruling recorded in the ingest.md amendment log.

title: AT-101's live-tree ban covers `git stash`/`git checkout` against COMMITTED work but says nothing about uncommitted files; the T-131 maker restored a sabotage with `git checkout` on an uncommitted prompt and destroyed its own in-progress rewrite. evidence: Reported in `qa/manifests/t131-ingest-persists.md` ('An accident I caused and am reporting rather than hiding'): restoring sabotage C, `git checkout src/autotester/prompts/ingest_video_v1.md` reverted the whole uncommitted rewrite, caught because `grep -c NARRATION` returned 0, then retyped. Checker verified independently that nothing was in fact lost: `git diff 1c8c8e4^ 1c8c8e4 -- src/autotester/prompts/ingest_video_v1.md` is a coherent 29-line addition carrying the complete 'What the person said' section (ground truth, align not re-transcribe, do not paraphrase, the fabricated-quote rationale), the url/fields/screenshot_ts rules and the open_questions rule; `grep -c '{{NARRATION}}'` = 1 and the three sabotage-C tests pass -- this is a full rewrite, not a degraded retype. title: `load_sidecar`'s `except (OSError, ValueError)` does not cover the malformed shapes its own docstring promises to survive, so a bad `<video>.transcript.json` crashes `autotester ingest run` with an unhandled traceback.
evidence: stages/ingest.py:130-131 catches only (OSError, ValueError). schema/media.py:44 `raw.get("segments", [])` raises AttributeError when the sidecar's top-level JSON is not an object; media.py:45 `TranscriptSegment(**seg)` raises TypeError when `segments` holds non-mappings. Neither is an OSError or a ValueError. Reproduced by the checker end-to-end through CliRunner on the real `app` at c4c878a: sidecar `[1,2,3]` -> `ingest run` exit=1, AttributeError; sidecar `{"segments":["hi"]}` -> exit=1, TypeError. The docstring three lines above the except reads "a malformed sidecar must not stop an ingest, because a reading with no narration is still worth having" -- a guarantee declared, plumbed, and not applied by the path that ships, which is the exact defect shape this unit exists to close. Latent on the current corpus: all 10 real *.transcript.json files are `{segments:[{start,end,text}], speech_seconds}`. Fix direction: catch the parse broadly (or validate the decoded top-level shape before touching it) so the fallback is genuinely best-effort; closing AT-134 at the same time makes the degradation audible.

title: A sidecar the loader rejects degrades silently to the prompt asserting "no speech detected" on a recording that HAS speech -- a confident false claim about ground-truth evidence, with nothing logged.
evidence: Executed by the checker through the real CLI at c4c878a: a sidecar `{"segments":[{"start":0,"end":2,"text":"real speech","confidence":0.9}]}` (one extra key; TranscriptSegment is extra="forbid") -> `ingest run` exit=0 and the rendered prompt contains "no speech detected". Nothing anywhere records that a sidecar was present and unreadable. Contract I8 requires the prompt to say no-speech WHEN NO SPEECH EXISTS; here it says it when speech exists. The maker's own AT-108/AT-114 sweep ruled that swallowing a cause is a defect, and that ruling applies to its own code. The reusable distinction: swallowing is acceptable when the fallback is NEUTRAL (a re-upload, an empty optional) and a defect when the fallback is an ASSERTION the reader will believe. Fix direction: keep the best-effort load, but emit one line on stderr naming the sidecar and the parse error; a future transcriber adding a `confidence` field must not silently blank the tester's own words.

title: Untyped refusals in the two new byte-identity paths: `verify_source_bytes` raises a raw PermissionError when the registered path is now a directory, and the AT-128 content cache key raises a bare FileNotFoundError from `upload_and_wait` where the old size key fell through to the SDK-wrapping try.

title: `is_capable_of_failing` fails OPEN by construction: it rejects a denylist of five known shapes and accepts everything else, so trivially unfailable commands sail through. Answering the maker's question: it CAN be made to fail closed, via an allowlist of task-specific forms plus an explicit written waiver.
evidence: Checker probe at b0b3eb3, predicate driven over 17 candidate commands. Accepted (False negatives, all unfailable or repo-wide): 'echo done'; 'uv run python -c "pass"'; 'test -f README.md'; 'uv run pytest --collect-only tests/test_x.py' (measured exit 0, collects without running); 'ls src/autotester/stages/merge_flowspec.py || true'; 'cat qa/contracts/ai-target.md > /dev/null || exit 0'; 'true # tests/test_x.py'; and the pytest-directory family filed separately as AT-154. Structural cause 1: the segment splitter is `command.replace('&&',';').split(';')` -- it does not split on `||`, so a `|| true` or `|| exit 0` suffix is invisible and any command can be neutered by appending one. Structural cause 2: `_is_repo_wide` returns False for every command it does not recognise, and `is_capable_of_failing` is `any(not repo_wide)`, so an unrecognised segment is scored as PROOF of task-specificity. Not filed as a FAIL of at141-at115: the manifest declares the heuristic and asks for exactly this list. Concrete fail-closed design (the better unit the maker asked for): invert to an ALLOWLIST evaluated per segment -- a segment is accepted only if it is (a) `check_deliverable.py` with at least one --exists/--contains, (b) pytest naming a part ending `.py` or containing `::` and NOT carrying --collect-only, or (c) `python scripts/<name>.py` with at least one argument; reject any command containing `||`; and give a task an escape hatch of `done_check.waiver: "<why a repo-wide command is right here>"`, which the test asserts is non-empty. Unknown shape is then rejected rather than accepted, and the hole becomes a greppable written decision instead of a silent pass.

title: The allowlist still admits four families of unconditionally-passing commands, because `_is_task_specific` matches tokens ANYWHERE in the command instead of at the program position, and disqualifies `||` but not a pipe.
evidence: Checker probe at ca18643 driving tests/test_goal_done_checks.py:is_capable_of_failing directly. Accepted (all exit 0 unconditionally): (1) `uv run pytest --co tests/x.py` -> True -- `--co` is pytest's documented short alias for `--collect-only`, which the code explicitly excludes one line away; this is the AT-154 shape recurring (the guard's own stated logic, defeated by a synonym). (2) `echo pytest tests/x.py` -> True and `uv run pytest tests/x.py | true` -> True and `uv run pytest tests/x.py |& true` -> True -- the segment splitter handles `&&`, `;` and `||` but not `|`, so a pipe neuters the exit status exactly as `|| true` did in AT-155. (3) `echo x #check_deliverable.py` -> True and `true # pytest tests/x.py` -> True -- shlex.split keeps the `#` comment tokens, so a trailing comment mentioning a recognised program is accepted; note the suite already pins `'true # tests/test_x.py'` as a must-REJECT, and adding the word `pytest` to that same comment defeats it. Root cause is one line, not three: the branch guards are `'pytest' in parts` / `'python' in parts` / `any(p.endswith('check_deliverable.py') for p in parts)` -- membership over ALL tokens, so any token anywhere (an echo argument, a comment, a pipe's right side) satisfies them. Fix direction: resolve the program token first (skip `uv`, `run`, and `-`-prefixed words, then take the first bare word) and match on THAT; split segments on `|` as well as `||`, `&&`, `;`; add `--co` to the collect-only exclusion. Not filed as a FAIL of at154-at157-fail-closed: the unit's claim is that the predicate now fails closed by default, which it verifiably does (five sabotages reproduced), and no task on disk carries any of these shapes.

title: The `|| true` neutering family still reaches through `;` and `&&`: `is_capable_of_failing` scores segments with any(), so a task-specific segment followed by an always-true segment is accepted even though the shell returns the LAST segment's exit code.
evidence: Checker probe at 62c3e65 driving tests/test_goal_done_checks.py:is_capable_of_failing directly. Accepted, all exiting 0 unconditionally: 'uv run pytest tests/x.py; true' -> True; 'uv run pytest tests/x.py && true' -> True; 'uv run pytest tests/x.py; :' -> True; 'uv run pytest tests/x.py; exit 0' -> True; 'uv run pytest tests/x.py && exit 0' -> True. Cause: is_capable_of_failing (line 115) normalises '&&' to ';', splits, and returns any(_is_task_specific(seg)) -- ALWAYS_TRUE is consulted only for the segment being scored, never for its siblings, so a no-op segment appended after a real one is invisible. Same family as AT-158's '| true' and AT-155's '|| true', reached through the two separators the splitter itself creates. Fix direction: reject the whole command when ANY segment is in ALWAYS_TRUE. Do NOT switch any() to 'the last segment must be task-specific' -- that would reject the legitimate on-disk shape 'check_deliverable.py --exists X && uv run autotester doctor' (T-126, T-150). No live instance: ';' appears in no done_check.cmd in .goal/goal.json and all six '&&' commands pair two real segments. Not filed as a FAIL of at158-at160-program-position: the unit's claims (program-position matching, the five sabotages, Z6 green at parent) all verifiably hold, and the checker ruled this should be QUEUED rather than fixed now.
note: MAKER: fixed in commit b91147a, checker PASS cycle 1 (qa/verdicts/at161-goal-neutering-any-segment.md, commit b668e49) - checker independently reproduced the sabotage in its own isolated extract and confirmed the rejected-alternative-fix reasoning holds. Filed a narrower residual: AT-359 (a ;-chain ending in a non-literal always-succeeding segment like echo/ls is still accepted) - outside this unit's own scope, not charged against it.

title: mtime_ns has ~0.5ms real granularity on this Windows host, so an idempotent write landing in the same filesystem tick as the baseline stat is still invisible - the residual of AT-186's fix, worth stating rather than assuming nanoseconds.
evidence: Checker of at185-at187-write-not-change cycle 1, measured on the host: 200 successive identical-byte writes to one file produced only 41 distinct st_mtime_ns values (min non-zero delta 479700 ns ~ 0.48 ms), and in a tight stat/write/stat loop 40 of 50 writes left st_mtime_ns UNCHANGED. So (mtime_ns, size, sha256) detects an idempotent write only when it falls outside the ~0.5 ms tick of that file's baseline stat. Not a live risk for either current test: the baseline walk stats and sha256s 1258 files before any command runs, and the observed sabotage-AX delta was 44.3 ms (1788892987910587700 -> 1788893032245811700). Filed low so the property is on the record and nobody later reads 'mtime_ns' as 'nanosecond-exact'. evidence: Checker of at176-at178-render-not-scan cycle 1. tests/advice_scan.py _module_constants() walks only tree.body of the file being parsed, so a name bound by `from ... import PREP_COMMAND` is not in `constants` and _render returns UNRESOLVED for it. Measured by running the collector directly on constructed sources: `from autotester.stages.media_prep import PREP_COMMAND` plus the verbatim media_prep construction f"run `{PREP_COMMAND} " f"{slug} {sid}` on the HOST first" yields **[]** -- not a partial render, not a warning, nothing. Same for a name that is not module-level at all: `def f(group): raise RuntimeError(f"run `autotester {group} prep x`")` yields []. That is precisely the AT-176 blind spot this unit closed, restored by an ordinary refactor of a constant whose entire purpose is to live in one place. Not raised high: measured zero live instances (all 9 collected sites today resolve same-module) and tests/test_media_prep.py's instance test still covers require_prepared directly. title: _is_documentation covers only ast.Expr(Constant), so a bare f-string or +-concatenated documentation statement is scanned as advice -- including this codebase's own variable-docstring convention if ever written as an f-string.
evidence: Checker of at176-at178-render-not-scan cycle 1. tests/advice_scan.py _is_documentation() filters `isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant)`, but the same commit taught advice_in() to scan ast.JoinedStr and ast.BinOp, and a bare JoinedStr/BinOp statement is also an ast.Expr. Measured on constructed sources: f"""the old name was autotester media prep and it is dead""" as a bare statement yields ['media prep and it is dead']; "the old name was " + "autotester media prep" + " and it is dead" yields ['media prep and it is dead', 'media prep']. The sharp case is the first: PREP_COMMAND's own variable-docstring exists to record that `autotester media prep` is dead, and _is_documentation's docstring claims it 'covers real docstrings and this codebase's variable-docstring convention' -- it covers the plain-Constant form only, so documenting a dead command in the f-string form would FAIL the guard it is supposed to be exempt from. Latent, not live: walked every .py under src/autotester with ast and found ZERO bare JoinedStr/BinOp statements, so the suite is green for a real reason. Fix direction: widen the exclusion to `isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant | ast.JoinedStr | ast.BinOp)` -- one clause, same rule (an expression statement's value is discarded, so the program can never hand it to anyone).

title: test_the_dialog_page_does_not_trap_the_crawl enumerates the two terminal statuses its author observed instead of asserting the invariant it is named for, so a load-induced aborted_error reds the adapter's own slot-1 verify.
evidence: Checker of at176-at178-render-not-scan cycle 1, folding the maker's qa/feedback-inbox.md entry. tests/test_explore_live.py:139 asserts `dialog_node.status.value in ('aborted_dialog','explored')`; NodeStatus has exactly three terminal values and the excluded third, ABORTED_ERROR, is the one a loaded host produces. CONFIRMED INTERMITTENT, NOT A REGRESSION: `git show --stat e2f119f` touches tests/ and .goal/ only -- no file under src/autotester/stages/explore* changed, so there is no code for a regression to live in -- and the checker observed 7 consecutive clean runs (3 full suites including both sabotage runs; 3 isolated runs of the file, 8 passed each; 1 isolated run executed CONCURRENTLY with a second full suite, 8 passed). Could not be reproduced even under deliberate load. RULING ON THE MAKER'S GENERALISATION: substantially right, imprecisely stated -- this test asserts membership in a TWO-element set, not 'one exact terminal NodeStatus', so the maker's wording would sweep in tests that are not brittle. The correct shape is narrower: a live test must assert the invariant it is NAMED for, not enumerate the outcomes the author happened to observe. Here 'does not trap the crawl' is already fully carried by `crawl.finished_at is not None` on the line above; whether the node aborted on the dialog or on a load-induced navigation timeout, the crawl was not trapped. EXPOSURE: `uv run pytest` is the adapter's slot-1 verify and every manifest in this project cites it, so a flaky member turns 'the suite is green' from a fact into a probability -- but the failure direction is a false FAIL on a loaded host, never a false PASS, so no verdict already given rests on it; the real cost is a maker or checker meeting an unrelated red suite and learning to re-run until green. Fix direction: assert the node reached SOME terminal status (not left pending/queued) plus finished_at, so the test fails when the crawl hangs -- the thing it exists to catch -- and not when a busy host times a navigation out.

title: adjudicate's sort key omits prompt_name, so in the SHIPPED two-prompt ensemble the merge is order-dependent -- VL4's own property, falsified, with the determinism test structurally blind to it.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 1. stages/adjudicate.py:190 sorts by (offset_s, provider_label, chunk_index). PROMPT_NAMES in stages/analyze_video.py has TWO entries, so for one model and one chunk the two prompts' observations are EQUAL under that key; Python's sort is stable, so the tie is resolved by the caller's list order. Measured: two ModelObservations identical but for prompt_name (the mapping pass carrying screens/purpose/url, the issues pass carrying an issue and a different summary) produce 2 DISTINCT contents across the 2 permutations, differing in `screens`, `journey`, `issues` AND `summary` -- i.e. every first-seen-wins merge (_merge_lists union order, `url`, `purpose`, `narration`, the summary join) inherits the caller's order. title: video_issues_v1.md never mentions the `confidence` field while instructing the model to take every spoken remark at its word, so a weak finding has no channel to be marked weak -- and adjudicate only ever raises confidence, never lowers it.

The prompt correctly forbids the three failure modes that matter -- inventing ('Report only what you can point at'; 'Anything you did not see or hear in this section'; 'return an empty list -- that is a real answer, and a normal one'), paraphrasing narration ('verbatim from the transcript below. Each is independently evidenced: sabotage BN (unsliced narration) fails 2 tests and BO (dropped offset) fails 1. The false-positive risk is elsewhere. schema/observation.ObservedIssue declares `confidence: Confidence = MEDIUM`, and the prompt names screen/t_start/category/severity/title/what_is_wrong/on_screen_text/narration/origin -- but never confidence. The predicted failure at scale is a sheet of HIGH-confidence S2 rows derived from asides. Fix direction: give the model the confidence field explicitly with a rule tied to evidence (spoken-and-screen -> high, a single unelaborated aside -> low), and consider requiring agreement across DIFFERENT prompts, not merely different models, before HIGH.

title: VideoAnalysis.observations_used/expected and is_complete reach no reader: nothing in the CLI, the exported sheet or the UI surfaces a partial analysis, so the coverage numbers discharge VL3 on disk while a human still cannot see that they are holding a fragment.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 2. AT-198's fix is real and correct -- a crippled run persists observations_used=1 / observations_expected=12 into the analysis JSON (checker measured it end to end, 2 providers x 2 prompts x 3 chunks with one provider dead and the other dying after its first call). The only consumers anywhere are two tests (tests/test_adjudicate_determinism.py::test_a_partial_reading_says_how_partial_it_is and tests/test_analyze_cache.py::test_the_analysis_records_how_many_calls_it_is_missing). No CLI command prints it, stages/issues.py's 13-column export has no column and no banner for it (correctly -- the sheet's shape is the tester's), and src/autotester/ui/ never mentions it. `is_complete` is additionally a @property, so it is NOT serialised into the persisted JSON (checker confirmed 'is_complete' is absent from the analysis file's keys) -- a downstream reader must recompute it. Belongs with T-136, which is the first unit that computes a number against this artifact.

title: adjudicate(..., expected=None) defaults observations_expected to observations_used, so any caller other than analyze() gets an artifact that silently declares itself complete -- a default-value fallback inside the very field added to stop one.
evidence: Checker of t133-ensemble-and-issues cycle 2. stages/adjudicate.py:209 writes `observations_expected=len(shifted) if expected is None else expected`. analyze() always passes the real product (len(providers) * len(PROMPT_NAMES) * len(prep.chunks)), so today the shipped path is honest and this is latent. But adjudicate() is a public, pure function and the stated next consumer is T-136's scorer, which re-adjudicates cached observations; a re-adjudication over a partial observation directory would produce used == expected and `is_complete is True` for a fragment -- exactly the untruth AT-198 was filed about, now with a field stating it affirmatively rather than a field being absent. The keyword is optional and the default is the one value that can never be wrong-looking. Measured: adjudicate([one_observation], 'src_1') -> observations_used=1, observations_expected=1, is_complete=True. Fix direction: make `expected` required (it has exactly one production caller, so the change costs one line), or default it to 0 -- `is_complete` already returns False on expected==0, which is the correct reading of 'nobody told me what was intended'. Filed medium: no live instance, and the honest value is supplied on the only path that ships. || CHECKER 2026-09-09 (t136-scorer cycle 1): FIXED. stages/adjudicate.py:229 now writes `observations_expected=0 if expected is None else expected`; is_complete requires expected>0 so it reads 0 as not-complete. Sabotage SJ (restore len(shifted)) in an isolated git archive HEAD extract fails exactly 1 test (test_omitting_expected_records_UNKNOWN_not_complete) -- live guard, not decorative. Sole production caller stages/analyze_video.py:181 still passes the real product; no regression. Moves to `verified` only on a later re-check.

title: The force-before-read half of the AT-199 fix is unevidenced: reverting observe_chunk to consult the cache before testing `force` fails 0 tests, because skip_unreadable alone now carries the whole crash-safety promise.

Fix direction: one test that corrupts a cached observation and asserts analyze(force=True) both completes AND re-requests every chunk -- the checker ran exactly that by hand and it passes (12 calls), so it is a test that exists only outside the repo.

title: scripts/score_video_issues.py:92 resolves its default project root to `D:\` (repo_root().parent.parent), so the shipped command reads D:\projects\erp\issues.jsonl -- outside the repo. The manifest's central 'exit 2 proves it can fail' evidence is produced by this bug, and T-136's done_check can never pass.
evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1. `root = args.root or ProjectPaths(args.project).root.parent.parent`. Measured (.work/chk-t136/probe5.py, live tree): repo_root() = D:\autoTesting; the expression = D:\; ProjectStore('erp', D:\).paths.issues = D:\projects\erp\issues.jsonl; the correct path is D:\autoTesting\projects\erp\issues.jsonl. Consequences, in order of severity: (1) the refusal the whole manifest is built around ('project erp has no derived issues... 7 truth rows', exit 2, reproduced by the checker against the real Trainers sheet) is NOT evidence that projects/erp has no issues -- the same message and the same exit code would be produced against a fully populated project, so the maker's claim that the exit code demonstrates the scorer 'can fail for the right reason' is unsupported; (2) T-136's done_check in .goal/goal.json runs the command with NO --root and expects exit 0, so the task is structurally incapable of closing even after a vision credential arrives; (3) if D:\projects\<slug>\ ever exists (a second checkout at a different depth), the scorer silently scores a DIFFERENT project's issues against this project's truth sheet. Why no test caught it: every invocation in tests/test_score_cli.py passes `--root str(root)` (line 76), so the `args.root or ...` fallback -- the only branch that ships -- is executed by nothing in the suite. Fix direction: `root = args.root or repo_root()` (core/paths.repo_root, already honours AUTOTESTER_ROOT for tests), plus one test that runs the done_check invocation verbatim and asserts the path opened is inside the repo.

title: The scorer's refusal names `autotester issues derive`, a command the CLI does not expose -- and no command anywhere derives video issues. Fifth instance of the AT-163/172/176/206 dead-advice class, landing in scripts/, which the class-level guard does not scan.
evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1, run against the live CLI. `uv run autotester issues derive --help` -> `No such command 'issues'`; `uv run autotester --help` lists doctor/providers/map/snapshot/login/explore/approve/ledger/flowspec/report/ingest and no `issues` group; `uv run autotester ingest --help` lists register/list/prep/frames/run. Beyond the name being wrong, there is no right name: `grep -rn 'derive_issues' src/` returns the definition at stages/issues.py:78 and one docstring mention -- NO caller under src/, so nothing in the shipped surface can produce projects/<slug>/issues.jsonl at all. Why the existing guard is blind to it: tests/test_cli_advice_resolves.py:47 sets `SRC = parents[1]/'src'/'autotester'` and every collection goes through advice_in_source(SRC), so scripts/ is outside the scanned tree; a repo-wide grep for DERIVE_HINT returns exactly two sites, both inside scripts/score_video_issues.py. The constant's own docstring claims 'Named once so the advice-collector guard can see it and the CLI-resolve test can prove it is a command that exists' -- false in both halves. The only test on the message is `assert 'issues derive' in result.stderr` (tests/test_score_cli.py:98), a substring assertion, which VL1d states verbatim does not evidence the criterion. Fix direction: point the advice at a command that exists (or build the derive command as its own unit), and extend the collector's roots to scripts/ so the class-level guard covers the operator-facing surface that is not a library.

title: stages/score.py::score is order-dependent on the issue list: `max()` returns the FIRST maximum, so a tie hands the choice to store.list_issues() file order and RECALL ITSELF moves. AT-197's class, in the module that computes the north star's number.
evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1. score.py:219 `best = max(candidates, key=lambda c: (c[0], -c[1]), default=None)`; candidates are built by iterating `remaining`, which is `list(issues)` = the order ProjectStore.list_issues() read them off issues.jsonl (append order). The manifest asserts 'the ordering is deterministic because candidates sort on similarity then time' -- that is true only where the pair (similarity, -seconds_apart) is unique. Measured (.work/chk-t136/probe4.py): truth rows T1='cat dog' and T2='cat dot bird' both at 10s on erp1.mp4; issues X='cat dot' and Y='cad dog' both at 10s; similarity(T1,X)=similarity(T1,Y)=0.8, similarity(T2,X)=0.8, similarity(T2,Y)=0.6. With --threshold 0.7, issue order [X,Y] -> recall 0.5, order [Y,X] -> recall 1.0. At the default threshold 0.30 the recall coincides but the CLAIM does not: probe2 case B shows the per_row entry for T1 naming issue X or Y purely by list order, so `matched_title` and `similarity` in the JSON report are order-dependent under the shipped defaults. Ties are reachable in the shipped system: the ensemble is two models x two prompts and join_issues merges only within a window, so near-duplicate reports at the same second are exactly what it produces. This is the defect class that cost T-133 a fix cycle (AT-197: a sort key with ties handing the decision to caller order) and that VL4 was tightened for; the scorer is the module where it costs a number a human is asked to trust. Fix direction: make the candidate key total (append the issue id as a final tiebreak), or sort `remaining` on a content key before matching -- and pin it with a permutation test over the shipped shape, the way test_adjudicate_determinism.py does for VL4.

title: scripts/score_video_issues.py::coverage skips a contributing source whose analysis is absent from disk, so `complete: true` is reachable while a scored source's reading is entirely unknown -- AT-207's own untruth, reintroduced at source granularity inside AT-207's fix.
evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1. coverage() line 53-54: `analysis = store.load_analysis(source_id); if analysis is None: continue` -- the source contributes issues to the score but nothing to the coverage totals, and `complete` is computed as `not partial and expected > 0` over the sources that happened to load. Measured end to end (.work/chk-t136/probe7.py, temp root, real ProjectStore/JSON files): two sources each contributing one issue, analysis.json saved for source 1 only (used=4/expected=4), one truth row -> exit 0 and coverage {observations_used: 4, observations_expected: 4, complete: true, partial_sources: []}. Source 2's reading is not partial and not zero -- it is unknown -- and the report affirmatively states the run was complete. AT-207 was filed because 'a recall from 1 of 12 model calls is otherwise indistinguishable from one taken from 12 of 12'; a missing analysis is the same indistinguishability one level up, and the manifest claims this unit 'names partial sources and says whether the run was complete'. The maker did get the all-zero case right: with no analysis at all, expected=0 and complete is False (measured). Fix direction: count sources without an analysis into a third list (e.g. `sources_without_analysis`) and let any entry in it force `complete: false` -- silence is not coverage.

title: recording_key splits on the first '(' and falls back to the raw cell, so distinct recordings collapse to one key (`clip (1).mp4` and `clip (2).mp4` both -> `clip`) and an empty/None cell becomes `''`, which is matchable -- two unknown recordings score as the same recording.
evidence: Checker of t136-scorer cycle 1, measured directly (.work/chk-t136/probe1.py): 'clip (1).mp4' -> 'clip'; 'clip (2).mp4' -> 'clip'; 'erp (final) cut.mp4' -> 'erp'; 'report (v2).mp4 (Divya)' -> 'report'; '' -> ''; None -> ''; '  ' -> ''; 0 -> ''. `clip (N).ext` is the exact name Windows and Chrome give a duplicate file, so the collision is not exotic. The absence case is the sharper one: unlike the `At` column -- where the maker correctly refuses an unparseable cell BECAUSE second zero 'matches whatever happens to open the recording' -- a blank recording cell is accepted silently and produces a key that CAN match. Measured end to end (.work/chk-t136/probe6.py, temp root): a truth sheet whose Clip column is empty in every row, scored against two issues with an empty recording_label, exits 0 with recall 1.0, found 2, false_positives 0. title: A near-miss and a no-candidate-at-all are indistinguishable in the scorer's report: Match discards the rejected best candidate, so both print sim=0.00 dt=None.

title: AT-276 introduces its OWN false-positive mode: stopwording content-bearing action words can strip a short bug report down to near-nothing, inflating similarity() to 1.0 for genuinely unrelated faults

Mechanism: containment = |shorter & longer| / |shorter|; a word removed from STOPWORDS that occurred ONLY in the shorter text shrinks the denominator without shrinking the numerator, which can only raise the score. AT-232 (33 words) was purely grammatical/domain boilerplate (field/validation/screen/edit); AT-276 added many CONTENT-bearing action words (export/downloads/corrupted/when/large/count/update/filter/message/change...) that can legitimately be the entire distinguishing content of a short report. Under AT-276 STOPWORDS (this unit): 1.0 -- every word in the shorter sentence except "certificate" is now stripped (export/downloads/corrupted/when/large all newly stopworded), leaving shorter={"certificate"}, shared={"certificate"}, ratio 1/1. title: url_template is not idempotent across the keep_host boundary, so every screen learned from a VIDEO was invisible to coverage and its routes looked permanently unknown
evidence: core/urls.py's own docstring promised `url_template(url_template(u)) == url_template(u)`. It was false: urlsplit('demo.test/x') has no '//', so the HOST lands in .path and becomes a path segment. Reproduced against production code before the fix: url_template('https://demo.test/students/42') -> 'demo.test/students/{id}' (what stages/ingest.py stores, per ingest.md I7), and url_template of THAT with keep_host=False -> '/demo.test/students/{id}', while the observed URL reduces to '/students/{id}'. stages/coverage.py::_known_paths re-templates every stored url_pattern exactly that way, so a FlowSpec containing a screen for precisely the URL a run visited still reported a CoverageGap ['/students/{id}']. Crawl-learned screens were unaffected (explore_merge stores host-less), so the defect was specific to video-learned screens - the north star's own input.
note: Fix REPLACED in cycle 2 after both checkers and the engineering review converged: inferring host-ness from a schemeless string is unwinnable in principle ('settings.json' and 'example.com' are the same shape), and the first attempt silently DELETED path segments ('settings.json' -> '/'). Root cause was never the parser: stages/ingest.py and stages/product_map.py stored url_pattern HOST-FUL while stages/explore_merge.py and stages/screen_identity.py stored it HOST-LESS, so ingest.md I7's stated purpose ('a screen learned from a video and the same screen found by a crawl collapse to one row instead of two') was DEFEATED - the two seams could never produce the same pattern. Cycle 2 deletes the heuristic and canonicalises all four producers to keep_host=False; re-templating a path is idempotent with no guessing. BLAST RADIUS CORRECTED: the maker's cycle-1 claim that no data was affected was FALSE - it measured projects/*/flowspec.json only. projects/erp/screenmap.json carried 3 video-derived rows mangled to '/vidysea.com/erp/trainers', rendered live on /projects/erp/product-map. Repaired in cycle 2 to '/erp/trainers' (backup .work/screenmap.json.bak). Defended by tests/test_ingest_persist.py::test_a_video_screen_and_a_crawled_screen_of_one_url_produce_one_pattern - the cross-seam assertion I7 always required and never had. || REOPENED by checker A cycle 2 and addressed in cycle 3 via AT-294 - see that row. title: A mutation can escape the sandbox: an absolute or ../ `file` path makes scripts/mutation_check.py write OUTSIDE its copytree
evidence: Checker's own attack against 55efeac. `target = work / mutation['file']` performs no containment check, and pathlib join semantics DISCARD `work` for an absolute path: work / 'C:/.../victim.py' -> 'C:/.../victim.py'; work / '../../x.py' -> the temp root. Driven end to end: with an absolute `file`, the harness read, mutated and rewrote a decoy file outside the sandbox, then reported killed=False exit=0 because the mutation landed where the sandboxed suite never imports (a false SURVIVED plus a live-tree write). A ../../ path onto an EXISTING outside file did the same; onto a nonexistent one it raises a bare FileNotFoundError rather than a MutationError, so the run dies with an unhandled traceback instead of a refusal. This falsifies two stated claims: _sandbox's docstring ('so a mutation can never touch the live tree') and the manifest's 'Mutations run in a copytree OUTSIDE the repo'. tests/test_the_live_tree_is_never_touched does not catch it - it only exercises a well-formed relative path. Certification direction is safe (false SURVIVED, never false KILLED); damage direction is not - a live file is rewritten, and if the process dies between the mutation write and the restore it stays mutated. In a repo whose AT-149/AT-150 history is path containment, this is the finding that most deserves a test.

title: The modal crawl is non-deterministic: ~1 run in 14 loses the dismissed-dashboard screen after exploring past it, and the flake lands in a test the mutation harness needs green.
