Source was byte-identical to the run that had passed minutes earlier. | Measured attempts to reproduce, all GREEN: 6 direct run_crawl probes (.work/flake_probe.py), 3 sequential `pytest tests/test_explore_modal.py`, 1 harness-style invocation (`-o addopts= -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider`), 3 concurrent pytest processes to force CPU contention. 13 green, 1 red. | Suspected mechanism, NOT confirmed: returning to the dismissed-dashboard node always requires the replay path, because a reload restores the veil -- so `return_to` must go go_back -> goto -> replay(return to the veiled node, click the mood button). Each rung is attempted exactly once with no tolerance for a page that has not finished re-rendering; `settle` is networkidle plus a fixed 500 ms grace. `go_back` may also restore the dismissed DOM from bfcache on some runs and re-run the document on others, which would make which rung succeeds vary between runs.

title: AT-076 goto() wires resolve_for_navigation() into check_destination(), whose NavigationRefused exception message embeds the raw resolved URL -- when a secret-bearing navigate target is refused for being outside project.allowed_domains, the exception message contains the cleartext secret value and is persisted unredacted to disk via two separate paths.
evidence: src/autotester/browser/session.py:61-66 check_destination(project, url) raises NavigationRefused(f"'{url}' is outside allowed domains {project.allowed_domains}") -- called at session.py:141 as check_destination(self.project, real) where real is the SECRET-RESOLVED value from resolve_for_navigation (session.py:140), not the placeholder. This call happens BEFORE _record()/redactor().scrub() ever runs (goto only calls _record on the success path, session.py:143), so this specific message never passes through the Redactor. Reproduced standalone (isolated git-archive HEAD extract, own uv venv): a secret whose own SecretRef.domains permits a host outside project.allowed_domains resolves successfully via resolve_for_navigation, then check_destination raises with the full resolved URL verbatim in the message (confirmed token SUPERSECRETTOKEN123 present in str(exc)). Two real persistence sinks for that unredacted message, neither of which scrubs: (1) stages/execute.py:82-85 run_case catches it via the generic except Exception (NavigationRefused is not special-cased there) and stores error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}" into RawResult, written by store/project_store.py:150-151 save_result -> write_json(run_dir/<case_id>.json, result) with no redactor call anywhere in that path; (2) stages/explore_node.py:119-120 and :128-130 catch NavigationRefused and pass str(exc) into record_edge()/add_issue(), persisted via store/crawl_store.py:66-73 add_edge/add_crawl_issue -> append_jsonl with no redaction. This is a regression introduced BY this unit: before AT-076, goto() never resolved secrets at all, so check_destination could only ever see a literal (non-secret) URL in its exception message. Wiring resolve_for_navigation ahead of check_destination in the same call chain, in a function whose own error message includes the URL verbatim, reopened the credential boundary this contract exists to hold (B4: Redactor masks every secret value in logs and artifacts -- this path bypasses the Redactor entirely). Manifest at076-navigation-secret-escape-hatch.md verified only that _record scrubs evidence on the success path; it never traced check_destination's own exception message, and no test in test_browser_navigation_secrets.py or test_secrets.py asserts an exception message is free of the raw resolved value (test_goto_still_refuses_a_resolved_destination_outside_project_domains only asserts pytest.raises(NavigationRefused), never inspects str(exc)).
expected: check_destination (or goto specifically) must not embed a resolved value that may contain a raw secret into its exception message -- e.g. raise with the HOST only (already computed) rather than the full url, or scrub the message through the SecretStore redactor before raising/propagating. Also: execute.py should special-case NavigationRefused for a secret-bearing target (or scrub error/hitl_prompt strings through secrets.redactor() generically before persistence in _result), and explore_node.py should scrub str(exc) before it reaches record_edge/add_issue. A regression test should assert the resolved secret value is absent from the exception message, from RawResult.error, and from the persisted CrawlIssue/ScreenEdge -- not just that NavigationRefused is raised.
checker_note: Sweep 2026-09-27: re-verified live in current tree (code + comments cite the fix by this AT id); falsified in an isolated scratch copy (real repo never edited) by reverting the fix and confirming test_goto_still_refuses_a_resolved_destination_outside_project_domains goes RED, then restored and confirmed GREEN. fixed -> verified.

title: goto()'s secret-resolution regression (AT-076) also reaches explore.py's login-precheck and seed navigation -- a generic Exception from a secret-bearing goto() (e.g. a real Playwright net/timeout error, which embeds the destination URL verbatim) is stored unscrubbed into Crawl.stop_reason and persisted to disk via save_crawl.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore.py:125-143 _already_past_login(rt, login_url) calls rt.session.goto(login_url) (line 135); login_url is login_step.target from the human-authored login Case's own NAVIGATE step -- exactly the 'a project's own login URL held as one .env value' scenario the AT-076 manifest itself names as the motivating case for resolve_for_navigation, so login_url is a realistic {{SECRET:KEY}} target. Its generic `except Exception as exc: rt.login_precheck_error = f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}'` (line 140-141) does not special-case NavigationRefused (already fixed) and does not scrub -- any OTHER exception goto() can raise (a real Playwright TimeoutError/net:: error, which characteristically embeds the destination it was navigating to, e.g. `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET at <url>` or `Timeout ...ms exceeded ... navigating to "<url>"`) reaches this handler carrying the fully-resolved (secret-bearing) URL verbatim. Same shape at src/autotester/stages/explore.py:156-165 _seed's `except Exception as exc: rt.seed_error = f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}'` for rt.session.goto(rt.project.base_url) (less likely to be secret-bearing in practice, since base_url is typically a plain project URL, but the field is `str` with no such constraint enforced anywhere). Both errors are unscrubbed strings that reach disk: `_login_failed_reason` (explore.py:190-197) folds rt.login_precheck_error into the string returned as rt.stop_reason (via run_crawl line 293), and _seed's own failure sets `rt.stop_reason = f'could not open base_url -- {rt.seed_error ...}'` directly (explore.py:296); `_finish` (explore.py:214-230) writes `crawl.model_copy(update={'stop_reason': rt.stop_reason, ...})` and calls `store.save_crawl(crawl)`, and crawl_store.py:28-29 `save_crawl` is `write_json(self.paths.crawl_manifest(crawl.id), crawl)` with zero redaction anywhere in that path -- the same unredacted-persistence shape AT-341 was filed for, just a call site this unit's fix did not touch. Reproduced standalone (own script against the live tree, a FakePage whose goto() raises RuntimeError('net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET at ' + url) exactly mimicking real Playwright's own message shape): calling explore._already_past_login(rt, '{{SECRET:PATHLYNKS_LOGIN_URL}}') against a secret resolving to https://app.pathlynks.test/login?token=SUPERSECRETTOKEN999 produced rt.login_precheck_error == "RuntimeError: net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET at https://app.pathlynks.test/login?token=SUPERSECRETTOKEN999" -- the token present verbatim. This is a regression from the SAME unit as AT-341 (before AT-076, goto() never resolved secrets, so a login-precheck exception here could never have carried one) -- a different call site (explore.py's login-precheck/seed, not execute.py's run_case or explore_node.py's edge/issue recording) that neither the cycle-1 nor cycle-2 fix traced.
expected: Either scrub rt.login_precheck_error / rt.seed_error (and anything folded from them into rt.stop_reason) through session.secrets.redactor() before they are stored on rt, or -- better, matching the C5/B4 pattern already used in execute.py::_result -- scrub crawl.stop_reason (and any other free-text Crawl field built from an exception) through the redactor at the one place it is written, _finish(), so every future caller of goto() inside explore.py/explore_return.py is covered by construction rather than by enumerating call sites again. A regression test should assert the resolved secret value is absent from rt.login_precheck_error / rt.seed_error / the persisted Crawl.stop_reason for a goto() failure that is NOT NavigationRefused.

title: AT-161 fix only rejects the three literal ALWAYS_TRUE tokens (true, :, exit 0) anywhere in a ;/&& chain -- a ;-chain ending in ANY OTHER always-succeeding segment (echo, ls) still neuters the real segment undetected.
evidence: Independently measured against tests/test_goal_done_checks.py::is_capable_of_failing at commit b91147a: is_capable_of_failing('uv run pytest tests/test_x.py; echo done') -> True, and is_capable_of_failing('uv run pytest tests/test_x.py; ls') -> True. Under real shell semantics, a `;`-joined chain's exit code is the LAST segment's exit code regardless of the earlier ones, so both commands above ALWAYS exit 0 (echo and a bare ls in an existing repo both succeed) no matter whether the guarded task is done -- the same neutering family AT-161 itself is about, just not one of the three literal tokens the fix checks for. The rejected alternative fix ("the last segment must be task-specific") would have correctly rejected both of these `;` cases (neither echo nor ls is task-specific) while still being wrong for `&&` chains for the reason AT-161's own evidence gives (T-126/T-150 -- check_deliverable.py && uv run autotester doctor, where the last segment is not task-specific but the first segment's failure still propagates as the overall exit code). Neither candidate fix is fully correct because the code normalises `&&` and `;` to the same split-and-score logic even though they have different exit-code semantics (`;` keeps only the last segment's code; `&&` short-circuits and propagates the first failure). AT-161's own manifest already discloses 'does not claim ... a complete shell-semantics parser', so this is filed as the next measured gap in the same family, not a FAIL of that unit.
expected: A more correct guard would treat `;` and `&&` differently: for a `;`-joined chain, capability-to-fail should require the LAST segment to be task-specific (only its exit code survives); for a `&&`-joined chain, ANY segment being task-specific is enough (since `&&` propagates the first failure). Today both separators are flattened into one split before scoring, which is what leaves this gap and what made AT-161's own fix possible in the first place.

title: scroll-invariance probe for visual_text: generate the shapes instead of imagining them
evidence: Stall diagnosis for at379 (qa/debug/at379-scrollable-pane-reachability-cycle3.md) put the failure on LOOP DESIGN: across three cycles every command the manifest lists was green â€” full suite, ruff, doctor, and both mutation specs â€” while a real in-scope false negative shipped each time. All five defects (AT-373/379/392/408/416) were found by a checker driving a browser at a shape the maker had no fixture for. All five violate ONE property: the multiset of glyphs visual_text reports must not change when the window or ANY scrollable container is scrolled anywhere in its range. Test it by PERFORMING the scrolls, not by computing offsets â€” computing offsets is the reasoning that lost five times. The sharpest evidence that the shapes must be generated rather than imagined: tests/fixtures/bidi_site/scrolled_panes.html already IS the AT-416 shape (overflow:hidden h=40 wrapping overflow:auto h=200); it cannot exhibit the defect only because the inner box does not overflow. One parameter changed and that existing fixture turns cycle 3 red. The shape was on screen and the one parameterisation chosen proves the opposite property. Scope: one browser test module over a generated corpus â€” overflow in {auto,scroll,hidden} x clip-path x nesting 1-3 x content-overflows in {y,n} x window-scrolled in {y,n}. Enumerate every scrollable container at runtime, drive each through {0, mid, max} per axis, assert the reported glyph multiset is identical in every state. Seed with the five known shapes. Test-only: no src/ change, so it cannot alter shipped detector output. The AT-416 case is expected RED and ships xfail(strict=True) so the suite stays green and the xpass is the signal when it is fixed. Honest limit: scroll-invariance is ONE-SIDED (a detector that reports everything is trivially scroll-invariant), so it pairs with the existing 'unreachable text is not reported' assertions rather than replacing them.
expected: A generated corpus that would have caught AT-373, AT-379, AT-392, AT-408 and AT-416 without anyone imagining the failing shape, and that turns the AT-416 direction question into a measurement.

title: visual_text reports text inside a `content-visibility:hidden` element, which a reader cannot see
evidence:
Found by the maker while reproducing AT-410, and deliberately NOT fixed in that unit. It is a separate defect with the opposite sign: a false POSITIVE, where AT-410 was a false negative. Measured in a fresh Chromium on a page holding `
CVHIDDEN_SENTINEL_92
`: the div's box is 1264x0; `div.checkVisibility()` returns TRUE; and `visual_text` returns `CVHIDDEN_SENTINEL_92` on the first and second call. `content-visibility:hidden` skips rendering the element's CONTENTS while its own box stays in layout, so checkVisibility() on the element itself is true. case AT-372 was written for works only because there the skipping happens on an internal slot, so the text's parent really does report false. Cost: the north star's false-positive term, and a genuine leak-detector false alarm on any page that hides content this way (a common lazy-render / virtualised-list pattern).

Check the ancestor chain's computed `contentVisibility`, not only checkVisibility() on the parent. Note the interaction with AT-410: `content-visibility:auto` must still be reported, including off-screen.

title: scripts/mutation_check.py._kill_tree's own cleanup proc.wait() has no timeout, and taskkill's failure is silently discarded (check=False), so a process the OS-level kill fails to remove would reproduce AT-487's exact unbounded hang one level down
evidence: scripts/mutation_check.py:147-153: `subprocess.run(["taskkill","/F","/T","/PID",...], capture_output=True, check=False)` (POSIX: `os.killpg`), then a bare `proc.wait()`. Checker review during at487 cycle-1 check: if taskkill does not actually terminate the process (a protected or unresponsive process, or a killpg race), nothing surfaces the failure and the trailing proc.wait() blocks indefinitely -- not exercised by any test here (an unresponsive-to-/F process is not practically simulatable), so not charged against at487's own claims, but a real residual gap in the fix's own safety net.
expected: Give the post-kill proc.wait() its own short timeout and raise/log distinctly if the process still has not exited after it (rather than a silent indefinite wait); consider asserting taskkill's exit code instead of discarding it.
source: qa/verdicts/at487-pytest-runs-are-bounded.md
fix_note: at490-491-tree-kill-is-bounded checked-PASS cycle 1 (commit 176a89c): proc.wait(timeout=KILL_GRACE_S=30.0) raises MutationError("...survived a kill of its process tree for 30s") on TimeoutExpired instead of waiting forever; test_a_process_that_survives_the_tree_kill_is_refused_not_awaited_forever reproduced red (bounded wait + raise, independently by checker in a throwaway copy) and green after. taskkill's exit code is still discarded by design -- the bounded wait is what decides, per the docstring; not the same as asserting the exit code, but the unbounded-wait hazard this issue names is closed.

title: check_qa_issue_rows / _is_marker_line are blind to an issue id named on a CONTINUATION line of a multi-line "**Issues addressed:**" list -- both the row-lost and row-stale checks silently skip it
evidence: _is_marker_line(line, marker) requires the LINE ITSELF to start with the marker text after stripping markdown decoration (src/autotester/ledger/checks.py:36-46); check_qa_issue_rows only scans lines for which that is true (lines 106-107, 115-116). A manifest that wraps its Issues-addressed list onto a second physical line -- which this repo's own manifests already do -- names ids that never reach either `named` (row-lost) or `claimed` (row-stale), because the wrapped line does not itself begin with the marker text. Reproduced live by instrumenting check_qa_issue_rows directly against the real manifest corpus (not by reading source alone): qa/manifests/at011-loop-md.md line 12 (`AT-027 (this cycle's fix -- cycle 1's Verify line didn't match qa/adapter.json verbatim)`), qa/manifests/at357-scope-sandbox-assertions.md (`AT-384 (high, cycle-1 FAIL) Ã‚Â· AT-385 (low, cycle-1 FAIL -- this manifest's own inaccuracies)`), and qa/manifests/at379-scrollable-pane-reachability.md (AT-392, AT-393, AT-394, AT-398, AT-408, AT-409, AT-411, AT-412) are all named on a continuation line and none of these 11 ids is ever added to `named` or `claimed` by a run of check_qa_issue_rows over the live tree. Currently inert -- all 11 ids checked have a live row today (`grep -c` confirms one row each) -- so no PASS to date rests on the gap. DIRECTION (checked, not assumed): this is a MISS, never a false accusation -- an id invisible to the scan cannot be added to `claimed` OR `named`, so it cannot trigger `ledger-row-stale` (over-accuse) any more than it can trigger `ledger-row-lost` (under-protect); it simply is not examined by either check. That keeps it on the safe side of C10's own stated preference ("an accusation it cannot support is worse than a gap"), but it still means the row-lost half of the invariant this exact function exists to enforce (AT-496's own docstring: "an issue a handshake artifact names must have a row") is silently unenforced for this shape. LIVE, not theoretical: the blind spot exists on real manifests on disk today (the three named above), it is only the CONSEQUENCE (an actual lost or stale row on one of those specific ids) that has not yet occurred. Checked and ruled out one candidate a reviewer suggested, `qa/manifests/at496-the-ledger-never-loses-a-row.md` line 12-13 ("AT-496 (medium, open -> fixed). Related, not closed here: AT-475 (rows living / only in the working tree) --"): that wrap does NOT demonstrate the gap -- AT-475 is named on the marker line itself (line 12), and the continuation (line 13) carries no id at all, so nothing is actually hidden there. This is the same module that has re-acquired a marker-scoping defect on every one of its last four units (AT-496 bare substring, AT-500 suffixed ids, AT-504 prose-about-the-marker, AT-508 fixed-vs-not-fixed) -- found while hunting per the AT-508 manifest's own provenance note that this function has not been read adversarially enough.
expected: Treat a multi-line "Issues addressed" block as one logical unit for scanning (e.g. keep consuming lines after a marker line while they don't open a new markdown block/heading and look like a continuation of the same list), rather than gating strictly on the single physical line the marker text appears on. Add a regression test with a manifest whose Issues-addressed list wraps a line, in both directions (a lost row and a stale claim on the wrapped line).

title: _NEW_FIELD's ALL-CAPS-label regex cannot match a field label that embeds a parenthetical before its colon, so such a label is invisible as a block boundary and the PRECEDING marker's block swallows it as a continuation -- the AT-509 fix's own over-run, reproduced live
evidence: src/autotester/ledger/checks.py:49 `_NEW_FIELD = re.compile(r"^[\s>#*_-]*[A-Z][A-Z0-9 -]*:")` requires the whole run up to the colon to be composed only of [A-Z0-9 -]; a label such as `**ISSUES KEPT OPEN (claimed fixed, not fixed):**` fails to match because of the parenthetical, comma and lowercase inside it, and it also fails `_is_marker_line` for the `ISSUES-WRITTEN` marker (does not start with that text). Reproduced live and directly against the shipped `_marker_lines('ISSUES-WRITTEN')` function (not a re-implementation) on qa/verdicts/at097-session-start-hook-regression.md lines 259-260: the block for the first `**ISSUES-WRITTEN:** AT-106, AT-107` marker incorrectly swallows the very next line, `**ISSUES KEPT OPEN (claimed fixed, not fixed):** AT-097, AT-029`, as a continuation -- so AT-097 and AT-029 are misattributed as named BY ISSUES-WRITTEN when they are actually named by a distinct, adjacent field. DIRECTION: over-inclusion, the same false-accusation shape AT-509's own fix exists to prevent (and the shape its 'Known limits' asked the checker to weigh independently for continuation prose -- this is a second, distinct mechanism producing the same shape: a field-boundary miss rather than prose-discussing-an-id). Currently zero consequence: both AT-097 and AT-029 already carry a ledger row (status: verified), so no `ledger-row-lost` fires and `claimed`/`ledger-row-stale` is not reachable for a verdict marker regardless (that computation only runs for kind=='manifests'). Checked for the mirror failure mode on the manifest side (a continuation line matching `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 ]*\([^)]*\):` immediately after `**Issues addressed:**`) across every qa/manifests/*.md file -- none found, so today's live exposure is verdict-only. Also confirmed the walk over-runs by one further line in the same direction for a different reason: when ISSUES-WRITTEN is the last field inside the standard fenced verdict block, the closing ``` delimiter matches none of the four stop conditions (blank/heading/_NEW_FIELD/marker) and is swept into the block too (qa/verdicts/at147-at148-grant-boundary.md, at355, at368, at386, t135-coverage-merge-expand.md and its .b.md all show this) -- harmless today because no id has ever been written on a fence delimiter line, but the same 'the stop-condition set is incomplete for real markdown shapes' root cause.
expected: Widen the stop-condition set in `_marker_lines`/`_NEW_FIELD` to recognize a field label that contains punctuation before its colon (e.g. match up to the first `:` on the line rather than requiring an uninterrupted ALL-CAPS run), and add a fenced-code-block-delimiter stop so a closing ``` cannot be swept into a block. Add a regression test pinning the at097 shape (`**ISSUES-WRITTEN:** ...` immediately followed by a differently-named field also carrying ids) so the block stops there rather than absorbing it.

title: Two concurrent checkers (at520-scripts-mapped-not-invisible, at521-finish-the-q-sweep) both had uncommitted edits to qa/issues.jsonl in the shared working tree at once; the at521 checker's `git commit --only qa/issues.jsonl` swept in the at520 checker's in-progress edits (AT-520 flip open->fixed, AT-525 append) alongside its own, landing them in commit 0fe2b6d before the at520 checker had written or committed its verdict

title: browser/assertions.py met() wraps the whole probe in contextlib.suppress(Exception) and returns True on error, and body_text() returns '' on a broken page -- an absent_text-only expectation on a crashed page records 'assert absent_text: met' and the run completes clean; the deterministic layer fails UNSAFE exactly where visible_text/dom_asserts fail safe

Ruled a defect, not contract-asked: D-032's Result asks for 'raises nothing' AND honest 'assert <field>: met|unmet' facts -- no-raise is satisfiable while failing SAFE (return False on probe error, name the error in the recorded detail); recording met from a swallowed exception is the false-PASS defence D-032 exists to provide, inverted. Secondary asymmetry: the url read at :59 is the module's only unsuppressed page read (met() wraps its copy; body_text/selector_exists swallow) -- if page.url raises on a closed page that line propagates, breaking assert_expected's own 'raises nothing' docstring.

source: qa/verdicts/at562-564-live-wiring.md cycle 1
title: UI case runs (ui/routes_runs.py::trigger_run) execute against the project's live target with no RunApproval check -- pre-existing, and deferred to T-122's live-case gate by qa/contracts/consent.md 'Out of scope'. Now that runs can fan out to N concurrent browser contexts (opt-in, Project.max_parallel > 1), RunBudget(None) leaves the whole run unbounded: D-018's 'nothing outward-facing starts without an approval' is not yet true for case runs.
evidence: master trigger_run checks only _require_declared_values; consent.md Out of scope: 'Gating ingest / expand / run_case -- T-122's live-case gate is a separate unit'; Project.max_parallel default 1; plan_parallel_run forces n=1 under ALLOW_WRITES (PR3).
expected: T-122 must not run live until trigger_run enforces a covering RunApproval and RunBudget(None) no longer means unlimited. Blocking, not advisory: the tier now permits mutation on production, so an unbounded unapproved run is reachable from the UI button. || FIX SHAPE SHARPENED (peer, verified): there is exactly ONE construction site -- stages/parallel_run.py:216-218 `def run_cases(..., *, approval: RunApproval | None = None)` feeding `RunBudget(approval)` at :225. The DEFAULT VALUE is the defect's delivery mechanism: a caller reaches unlimited by passing nothing. So making None mean zero is not sufficient -- the parameter must become NON-OPTIONAL at that seam, or a future caller re-acquires unlimited by omission. If None must stay accepted for test construction, it RAISES rather than returning an unbounded budget.
checker_note: RE-TRIAGED medium -> HIGH 2026-09-27 and made a T-122 PRECONDITION. Requested by the maker, verified independently, and the verification found the gap is WORSE than either of us had recorded. Two premises changed under this row without it being edited: (1) T-122 is a CASE run, not a crawl, so the first logged-in Pathlynks run takes precisely the path with no approval check; (2) Umesh named production Pathlynks the first target and authorized ALLOW_WRITES (qa/gates/write-policy-tier.md, D-053), so the pending allow_writes flip turns that unchecked path from a read into a MUTATION on production. THE NEW PART: it is not only that no check exists. stages/parallel_run.py:146-155 RunBudget treats a MISSING approval as UNLIMITED -- its own docstring says "None means no approval was supplied (unlimited)" and try_consume opens with `if approval is None: return True`. So the consent budget FAILS OPEN: a case run with no approval gets unlimited actions, unlimited wall-clock and unlimited probes, which is a guard that grants permission by the absence of permission. That is the core-invariants C12 principle inverted. Fix direction: ui/routes_runs.py::trigger_run refuses without a covering RunApproval BEFORE the first live case run, and RunBudget(None) must mean zero rather than unlimited -- an unbounded run should be impossible to obtain by omission. Verified by grep: approval|consent occurrences are 0 in ui/routes_runs.py and 0 in stages/execute.py, 13 in stages/parallel_run.py (all budget arithmetic, no gate).

source: checker Mode A of at590-doctor-optional-imports cycle 1 (adversary lens, reproduced by the checker)
title: at590's soft_import_ids (ledger/render.py) classifies an import as soft whenever the try's handlers name only ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError, without looking at the handler body. So `except ImportError: raise`, `raise RuntimeError('pip install x') from e` and `sys.exit('need x')` (the idiom for a REQUIRED dependency with a friendlier message) all exempt an undeclared hard dependency from C11's undeclared-dependency check.

expected: A try-guarded import is soft only when its ImportError handler degrades gracefully, meaning it binds a fallback or continues. A handler whose body ends by raising, or by calling sys.exit/exit, is hard. Add a test per shape (raise, raise from, sys.exit) plus a failing-first sabotage row (C7).

source: checker Mode A of at383-sessionstart-loop-status cycle 1 (security lens; reproduced by the checker)
title: at383's session-start hook kills only the `uv` process when loop-status times out. `$lsProc.Kill()` on Windows PowerShell 5.1/.NET Framework has no entireProcessTree overload, and `uv run` launches python as a child, so the python grandchild survives the kill. A hung loop-status leaves one stray process per session start.
evidence: Checker repro 2026-09-27 with the same ProcessStartInfo shape (FileName=uv, UseShellExecute=false, redirected, ReadToEndAsync, WaitForExit, Kill()): `uv run --project D:/autoTesting python -c <sleep 90>` was killed after 8s. The uv pid had exited, but the python pid (uv-managed cpython-3.11 python.exe) was still alive 1.5s later and had to be stopped by hand. [System.Diagnostics.Process].GetMethods() under powershell 5.1 lists only Void Kill().
expected: On timeout, kill the whole tree (e.g. `taskkill /T /F /PID $lsProc.Id`, or a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE). Add a test that starts a real grandchild through the same path and asserts it is dead after the timeout (the AT-494 shape in tests/test_flake_probe_real_process.py), plus a sabotage row (C7).

title: encode_chunks' new CHUNK_TIMEOUT_S=900.0 bounds a SINGLE chunk cut, but stages/media_prep.prepare loops it over the whole plan with no aggregate ceiling. A recording chunked into N pieces (chunk_minutes=3.0 default -> a 40min recording plans ~13-14 chunks) can still hang the INGEST stage for up to N*900s if ffmpeg is systemically broken (corrupt binary, full disk, driver fault) rather than wedged on one clip -- e.g. 13 chunks x 900s ~= 3.25h before prepare finally raises UnreadableRecording. The per-chunk bound is real progress (AT-639's original defect, an UNBOUNDED single call, is fixed) but the manifest's own framing ('so a wedged ffmpeg cannot hang INGEST forever') only holds for a single wedged instance, not a systemic one.

note: Not a defect in what AT-639 claims to fix (it fixes the single-call hang, verified). Filed because the manifest's own gap disclosure ('a CHUNK_TIMEOUT_S of 900s is a judgement, not a measurement') stops short of naming the aggregate exposure; a future unit could add a wall-clock deadline around the whole encode_chunks loop, or make media_prep.prepare bail after the first timeout without retrying further chunks (it already does not retry, so this is really about the plan's chunk count, not retries).

title: chunks.py:132's cleanup `path.unlink(missing_ok=True)` runs unguarded inside the except block that is about to re-raise the ORIGINAL ffmpeg failure. missing_ok=True only suppresses FileNotFoundError; on Windows a file just killed by subprocess.run(timeout=...) can still be transiently held by the OS or an AV scanner, so unlink can raise PermissionError ([WinError 32]). If it does, that new exception propagates in place of the original TimeoutExpired/CalledProcessError/OSError -- the `raise` statement on the next line never executes -- so media_prep.prepare's except Exception still catches it and still degrades to UnreadableRecording (AT-166 and C12 fail-closed both hold), but the persisted message's `type(exc).__name__` would read PermissionError instead of the real cause, obscuring why the cut actually failed.
evidence: src/autotester/media/chunks.py:125-133 (bare path.unlink(missing_ok=True) with no try/except around it, immediately before `raise`). Not reproduced against a real lock (would require pinning a file handle open across the unlink on this host); reasoning from documented Windows unlink-while-open semantics and the timing window between subprocess.run returning after SIGTERM/kill and the OS releasing the handle.
note: Behavior-preserving (fail-closed intact either way) -- filed as a diagnostics-quality issue, not a functional block. A fix would wrap the unlink in its own try/except OSError: pass so the ORIGINAL exception always survives to the raise.

title: BrowserSession._sweep_orphan_videos() (session.py close()) can delete a DIFFERENT, concurrently-running sibling case's already-finished video before it is renamed to safety -- in a real parallel run (plan.n > 1), which this unit itself wires as production behaviour.
evidence: stages/parallel_run.py::default_session_factory gives every parallel sibling session the SAME run_dir (AT-572 comment, confirmed ~line 245-259); browser/session.py::start() therefore computes the SAME `video_dir = run_dir / VIDEO_DIR_NAME` (_video_scratch) for every sibling, since it is derived only from run_dir. VideoMixin.end_case_video() finalizes a case's recording via three separate, non-atomic statements: (1) page.close() [writes the finished .webm into the SHARED _video_scratch], (2) Path(video.path()), (3) temp_path.replace(final_path). BrowserSession.close() (`if self.record_video: self._sweep_orphan_videos()`) does an unconditional `shutil.rmtree(run_dir / VIDEO_DIR_NAME, ignore_errors=True)` the moment ANY sibling session finishes ITS OWN case, with no awareness of siblings still recording into the same shared directory. Reproduced independently by the checker with real Chromium and real threading (two BrowserSession instances sharing one run_dir, each in its own thread mirroring stages/parallel_run.py::run_cases' ThreadPoolExecutor): thread B finalizes its page (finished .webm confirmed present on disk in the shared _video_scratch) and pauses via a threading.Event at the exact point end_case_video() would next call .replace(); thread A finishes its own case normally, renames its own video out cleanly, then calls session_a.close(). Output: 'scratch dir exists after A.close(): False' / "B's own temp file still present when B resumed (post-sweep): False" / 'B was able to rename its finished video to safety after the sweep: False' -- RACE CONFIRMED. Also confirmed the race window is realistically reachable, not contrived: stages/parallel_run.py::plan_parallel_run gives ram_slots = (measured_free_mb - 2048) // (512 + 128), which already evaluates to 2 on the very machine the checker ran this check on (~3.5GB free, per this dispatch's own machine note), i.e. plan.n=2 (triggering _run_cases_in_parallel, the vulnerable path) is the DEFAULT outcome on a moderately-loaded box, not a rare edge case.
expected: A FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE case's video must never be silently lost because an unrelated sibling case happened to finish first in the same run. Needs either: (a) a per-session-unique scratch subdirectory (e.g. `run_dir / VIDEO_DIR_NAME / <session-id>`) so no sibling's sweep can ever touch another sibling's in-flight files, or (b) `_sweep_orphan_videos` only ever removing files it can positively prove are orphans of THIS session (e.g. by tracking which random Playwright filenames this session itself created, never a directory-wide rmtree), or (c) making the finalize sequence in end_case_video atomic enough that no sweep can observe the half-finished state. This is new code introduced entirely by this unit (session.py _sweep_orphan_videos, video.py end_case_video) and the parallel-video wiring that exposes it (ui/routes_runs.py video_enabled=True, ui/run_execution.py record_video=True on the parallel path) is also new in this unit.
note: This is the reason t191-run-video FAILs cycle 1. The maker's own manifest correctly named this exact scenario ('a parallel run sharing the directory') as one of the four things the checker should attack hardest, and reasoned that it was safe ('every legitimate case video is already moved out of _video_scratch by the time close() runs') -- that reasoning holds only for a SINGLE session's own sequential cases, not for concurrent siblings sharing the same run_dir, which is exactly the shape stages/parallel_run.py already uses. | cycle-2 checker verification (2026-09-27): fix confirmed genuinely safe by construction, not by luck. `_video_scratch_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]` is minted once in `BrowserSession.__init__`, traced every construction path (serial shared session in ui/run_execution.py, dedicated entry-case session, and stages/parallel_run.py::default_session_factory's per-case `_factory`, which builds a brand-new BrowserSession per parallel case) -- no path reuses a session across two cases or calls start() twice, so the id is genuinely unique per case-run, not merely per code path. Reproduced the mandatory regression test's RED/GREEN independently in a git-archive throwaway copy OUTSIDE the bound worktree: (1) the manifest's own revert-style sabotage (scratch path back to bare VIDEO_DIR_NAME) -> RED, correct assertion; (2) a stronger stub-style falsification the manifest did not try -- constant _video_scratch_id instead of uuid4() -- also correctly RED, proving the test depends on per-session uniqueness, not merely on path nesting. Confirmed V1 (orphan-leak) stays genuinely closed under the new nested path by stubbing _sweep_orphan_videos to a no-op in the same throwaway copy: test_video_is_recorded_and_kept_only_for_fail_and_inconclusive_never_pass correctly reddens (3 stray files vs 2 expected), proving the narrower per-session sweep still does real work. Ran the new test 10x (6 quiet, 4 while a real full-suite run was active) with zero flakes -- the threading.Event-based ordering is deterministic under real load. Own full-suite run: 3 failed (2068 passed) -- test_no_pending_task_has_a_done_check_that_cannot_fail and test_revised_goal_contract_is_registered (ISS-at638-remainder-2, pre-existing .goal/goal.json drift, untouched by this unit's diff) plus test_run_once_kills_a_real_hung_process_and_its_real_grandchild (AT-627, load-sensitive, pre-authorized by the dispatch as non-chargeable when it fires) -- no fourth failure, nothing chargeable to this unit. The parent `_video_scratch/` directory is left behind empty (not rmtree'd) once all of a run's sessions close -- a cosmetic difference from the pre-fix behavior (which rmtree'd the whole bare dir), not a functional leak, since it is scoped to that run's own directory and holds zero bytes. Flipped open -> fixed; see qa/verdicts/t191-run-video.md cycle-2 section for the full account.

title: explore_replay.perform() never re-checks the destination host after a replayed fill/click, unlike explore_node.try_action (X7, explore_node.py:163) and explore_typing._type_one (explore_typing.py:69) which both call check_destination after EVERY action. explore_replay.py imports neither check_destination nor NavigationRefused, so a replayed edge that lands off-domain (a redirect, a compromised third-party script, dynamic page behaviour that differs from the original recording) is reported as a plain success and the browser is left on the off-domain page with no guard having fired.
evidence: src/autotester/stages/explore_replay.py imports (lines 30-37): Action, ElementRef, ScreenEdge, typing_allowed, typing_target_allowed -- no check_destination, no NavigationRefused. perform()/_issue() call rt.session.fill/select_option/click directly with no post-action host check. Reproduced with a probe (checker scratch, not committed): a fake session whose click()/fill() report current_url()="https://evil.example.com/phish" -- explore_replay.perform() returns None (success) and never calls check_destination (confirmed check_destination is not even an attribute of the module). Contrast: explore_node.py:162-166 and explore_typing.py:68-72 both wrap the equivalent point in try/except NavigationRefused and record OFF_DOMAIN_REFUSED. crawl-traversal.md's own 'Relationship to explore.md' section states X7 (host re-checked after every action) is 'byte-unchanged and still in force' for this contract.
expected: explore_replay.perform() (both the TYPED_ACTIONS branch and the click branch) should call check_destination(rt.project, rt.session.current_url()) after issuing the fill/select/click, exactly as explore_node.try_action and explore_typing._type_one do, and record OFF_DOMAIN_REFUSED (not a bare failure string) on NavigationRefused.
note: Filed on t165-crawl-traversal cycle 1, check B of the D-040 dual check. This blocks PASS: CR7/X7 both require the safety matrix to be byte-unchanged, and this is a real gap in the replay path specifically, not a pre-existing condition this unit merely inherited (explore_node and explore_typing both already carry this check; explore_replay.py is new to this unit and omits it).

title: PersonaScreen.key() is url_template-only (schema/portal_persona.py:74-77, predates T-165 at T-164), so two distinct SPA states sharing one URL -- the exact shape X3/X14 require to be recorded as two screens, and the shape the codebase's own feedback-inbox 2026-09-08 entry names as real ('index page filter toggle ... 7 screens across 6 url patterns') -- collide onto ONE key. evidence: Checker scratch probe (not committed): src/autotester/stages/portal_persona.py::_incoming_screens([node_a, node_b]) with node_a.url_template==node_b.url_template=='/dashboard' and different signatures returns len==1. src/autotester/stages/persona_changes.py::classify(existing_with_node_a_stored, [node_a, node_b], frontier_exhausted=True) returns {'new_screens': [], 'changed_screens': [], 'missing_screens': [], 'broken_screens': [], 'missing_unjudged': []} -- node_b appears in none of them. Root cause: PersonaScreen.key() (schema/portal_persona.py:74-77) returns url_template alone, unlike ScreenNode.id (screen_graph.py:79-82) which is content_id({t: url_template, s: signature}) -- structural identity via signature. persona_changes._reached() (persona_changes.py:93-102) does reached.setdefault(node_key(node), node) -- first node wins, second is silently dropped.

note: Filed on t165-crawl-traversal cycle 1, check B of the D-040 dual check. title: An incremental crawl (CR3) that skips its entry screen (or any node whose children are reachable only through it) never discovers those children this run, because explore_incremental.skip_unchanged short-circuits before explore_node.visit_node, and _enqueue (the only place a node enters rt.frontier.queue) runs only inside visit_node/_click_loop/try_action. The frontier then "exhausts" after representing only a handful of nodes, frontier_exhausted reads True, and persona_changes.classify() reports every other previously-known crawl-sourced screen as missing_screens -- CR4/D-040 acceptance test (c) explicitly requires zero missing entries when nothing was removed, and this fires on a byte-identical site.
evidence: Checker A live reproduction (headed Chromium, tests/fixtures/deep_site, not committed script at .work/checkerA_live_repro.py --incremental): crawl 1 (incremental=False) explores all 9 screens, 20 actions; build_portal_persona(store, crawl_id=first.id) seeds the persona; crawl 2 (incremental=True, same site, same bounds) matches and skips the entry screen "/" on its stored signature, never clicks anything, so no child screen is ever enqueued -- crawl 2 ends screens=1, actions=0, status=completed, stop_reason="frontier empty -- 1 screen(s) skipped as unchanged since the stored persona, and so NOT explored on this crawl". Running persona_changes.classify(persona, store.list_nodes(crawl2.id), frontier_exhausted=True) (checker scratch .work/checkerA_verify_missing_bug.py) returns missing_screens == ["/deep1.html","/deep2.html","/deep3.html","/deep4.html","/wide1.html","/wide2.html","/wide3.html","/wide4.html"] -- 8 of 9 known screens, none actually removed or even looked at. Confirmed the code path: explore.py::_bfs calls explore_incremental.skip_unchanged(rt, node) and only calls explore_node.visit_node(rt, node) when that returns False; explore_node.py::_enqueue (the only caller of frontier.queue.append) is reachable only from try_action, itself only from _click_loop, itself only from visit_node -- confirmed via grep, no other _enqueue/queue.append call site exists, and run_crawl never seeds the frontier from the persona index (grep for "incremental" in explore.py/explore_node.py shows only load_index and the two skip_unchanged/exhausted_reason call sites). No test in tests/test_persona_changes.py (all synthetic ScreenNode/PortalPersona fixtures) or tests/test_explore_completeness.py (incremental_pair never calls persona_changes.classify on its own crawl 2 graph) exercises this integration.

title: persona_changes._previously_broken() can re-report a continuously-broken screen as newly broken after intervening crawls whose own revision happened to have all-empty categories except unrelated ones, because it stops at the FIRST prior revision with ANY non-empty category and reads that revision's broken_screens as the whole history of what was already known broken, rather than accumulating broken-ever status across all revisions.
evidence: Checker A scratch reproduction (.work/checkerA_repro_broken_reset2.py, not committed): crawl 1 marks /a broken (revision 1: broken_screens=["/a"]); crawl 2 discovers /c new and does not re-observe /a's status change (revision 2: new_screens=["/c"], broken_screens=[]); crawl 3 re-observes /a still broken. _previously_broken() walks history in reverse, finds revision 2 first (non-empty because new_screens is non-empty), and returns its broken_screens field, which is empty -- so /a is NOT in was_broken, and classify() reports /a in broken_screens again on crawl 3 even though it has been broken continuously since crawl 1 and nothing about it changed.
expected: A screen once broken should stay off the broken_screens list on every subsequent crawl until it is observed non-broken again, regardless of what else changed in an intervening crawl -- i.e. was_broken should be the union of broken_screens across ALL prior revisions minus any later revision that observed the screen and found it not-broken, not just the first non-empty revision's own broken_screens field.
note: Filed on t165-crawl-traversal cycle 1, check A. Lower severity than ISS-3: this only causes a stale re-alert (noisy, not silent data loss), and requires a specific 3-crawl sequence to manifest, unlike ISS-3 which fires on the mainline 2-crawl incremental path. Not independently blocking on its own but adds to the CR4 completeness-honesty picture.

title: explore_safety.typing_target_allowed claims "never an upload, never a field whose own name marks it a password/credential field", but it can only test role plus a "password"/"passwd" substring on name+selector -- and browser/enumerate.js maps EVERY <input> that is not submit/button/checkbox/radio to role "textbox", including type="password" and type="file". enumerate.js computes the input's `type` and does NOT emit it, so ElementRef carries `tag` but no `type` and the Python gate structurally cannot see it. A real <input type="password"> whose name and selector avoid those two words (#pin, #otp, "Passcode") therefore passes the X10-b gate and is filled with a synthetic value on any run with write_policy in (test_account, allow_writes) and synthetic_typing=True.
evidence: src/autotester/browser/enumerate.js::roleOf -- `if (tag === "input") { ... return "textbox"; }` after only submit/button/checkbox/radio are special-cased; the emitted object (same file, the out.push block) carries {role,name,selector,enabled,visible,obscured,href,is_form_submit,in_row,target_blank,tag} and NOT `type`, although `type` is computed one line above for is_form_submit. src/autotester/schema/screen_graph.py::ElementRef has `tag: str` and no type field. src/autotester/stages/explore_safety.py::typing_target_allowed tests `el.role not in ("textbox","combobox","search")` then `"password" in label or "passwd" in label` over f"{el.name} {el.selector}".lower(). Checker B probe (t165-crawl-traversal cycle 2, throwaway git-archive copy outside the worktree): explore_replay.perform with a recorded TypedAction on ElementRef(role="textbox", name="PIN", selector="#pin") issues the fill (session.calls == [('fill','#pin','AT-165'), ('click','#go','')]) and returns None; same for name="Avatar", selector="#avatar". synthetic_values.synthetic_value's "pin" keyword branch returns str(1000 + n % 9000), so the value typed into a password input is a 4-digit number. The file-input half has a natural backstop that the password half does not: Playwright's locator.fill() rejects input[type=file], and explore_typing._type_one calls explore_replay.record only AFTER rt.session.fill() returns, so an upload is recorded as ERRORED and never enters rt.typed.

D-029's non-destructive clause is the authority: typing into a real password field can trip an account lockout on a live product, which is the class X10-b exists to prevent.

title: CR4's missing/changed still work at PersonaScreen.key() granularity, so when a product holds two (or n) structurally distinct states at one url_template and ONE is genuinely deleted while another survives, the deletion appears in NO category -- and because describe() then returns None, build_portal_persona's `if summary:` gate does not fire, so no PersonaRevision is written at all
evidence: Reproduced by checker A, cycle 2, in a throwaway git-archive copy outside the bound worktree, on a FULL exhausted non-incremental crawl (no skips): stored persona two states at '/' (sig-base, sig-panel) plus '/other.html' (sig-other), crawl reaching only sig-base and /other.html -> new [], changed [], missing [], broken [], missing_unjudged [], healthy [], describe() -> None. Generalises to n states with any subset removed while one survives. Control on the same evidence: deleting /other.html, which has its own URL, correctly yields missing_screens == ['/other.html'].
expected: A real deletion must reach some surface -- silence about one is the dishonesty CR5 exists to prevent. BUT the naive closure is REJECTED IN ADVANCE and a future unit must not take it: the rule 'a key whose reached signatures are a strict subset of its stored ones lost a state' fires identically on a state the crawl simply did not reach this run (typing off under X10-b, or the toggle never clicked), which the stored evidence cannot distinguish from a removal -- it would replace this silence with a fabricated deletion on every crawl of every two-state screen. A sound closure must record per-signature REACHABILITY evidence, not merely per-signature presence, and carry its own falsifiable test for the 'not reached this run' vs 'removed' distinction.

title: The approved T-169 measurement can produce an unmeasurable recall number, because of ORDERING. Umesh 2026-09-27: "tu apne side ki reports de dee mai humn side ki bnaa krr de dungaa baad mai" -- AutoTester's report is delivered FIRST and the human findings are authored afterwards. A ground-truth list written after reading the machine's output is anchored to it: the bugs AutoTester MISSED are exactly the ones such a list is least likely to contain, so recall is measured against a list partly derived from the thing being measured. False-positive rate survives this ordering; recall does not.
evidence: O6/intent.md:36 makes 'measured against an expert human tester on bugs found' the north star, and AT-281's approved done_check classifies every item match / miss / false-positive -- the 'miss' column is the one this ordering cannot populate honestly. schema/bench.py computes the scorecard from both columns, so a biased human column propagates straight into the headline trust number.
source: Umesh gate answer 2026-09-27 on the parallel-human ground truth
expected: Cheap fix, no extra human time, Umesh's choice of which: (a) he authors his findings BEFORE reading AutoTester's report -- the report can be written and held unread; or (b) he reads it first but marks each of his own items independent-vs-prompted, and recall is computed from the independent subset only with the prompted count disclosed. EITHER WAY the comparison artifact must RECORD the ordering that was used, so the trust number can never be quoted without it. A recall figure from an unrecorded ordering is the same class of defect as the coverage rounding this project refuses to do (O4). || STRENGTHENED 2026-09-27 (peer contribution, accepted because it makes the requirement fail closed and is therefore a C12 instance): the artifact must be able to emit "recall: unavailable (ordering not recorded)" and MUST do so rather than print a recall number whose provenance field is absent. Reason: a blank ordering field is silently read as "zero items prompted", which is the most flattering reading available and the one a missing field should never default to. So recall is not a number-with-a-caveat, it is a value that does not exist until its provenance does -- the same shape as core-invariants C12, "every health signal the loop reports must fail closed", and the same refusal as O4 coverage honesty. schema/bench.py must therefore treat recall as optional in its own model, not default it to 0.0. || SCHEMA GAP VERIFIED (checker, 2026-09-27): src/autotester/schema/bench.py has NO field for this anywhere. BenchTrial carries id, corpus_id, participant_label, findings, duration_s -- no ordering field, and Finding has no independent/prompted mark -- so BenchTrial.score() computes severity_weighted_recall UNCONDITIONALLY and there is no representable state in which it reports 'unavailable'. The requirement now has a contract home: qa/contracts/bench.md K7 (ordering recorded per finding, recall from the independent subset only) and K8 (unavailable, and NOT 0.0 -- a Pydantic default of zero is indistinguishable from a measured zero, reintroducing the same bias through the back door).
checker_note: Verified on disk 2026-09-27 that the maker acted on this before Umesh picked a fix, as advised: D-053 and the T-136a roadmap row both carry the ordering field, the independent-vs-prompted mark per human item, and recall computed from the independent subset only. This row stays OPEN until that artifact exists and a checker has re-derived it -- an entry in DECISIONS is a commitment, not a build. Umesh still owes the ordering CHOICE (author his findings before reading the report, or read first and mark each item), but the artifact is being built to record whichever he picks, so his answer is no longer on the critical path. [2026-09-27] Criteria written: bench.md K6/K7/K8 amendment. bench.md was amended rather than a new acceptance-comparison.md authored, because a new checker-authored contract needs a docs/DECISIONS.md Changes-authorized line and that append path is permission-blocked (ISS-at638-remainder-1); bench.md already governs schema/bench.py, the module that computes the number.

title: qa/issues.jsonl has no duplicate-id guard, and every id-keyed read of it silently keeps ONE row per id. Six of the ten documented collision pairs are status-divergent, so three findings that are `open` on disk (AT-548, AT-549, AT-552) are invisible to any consumer that builds a dict by id -- including doctor's own ledger loss-detector. The same repo raises on this for the OTHER ledger: ledger/store.py:22-28 rejects a repeated id in docs/FEATURES.jsonl ("rows are history, so a repeated id is a defect, not a merge"). qa/issues.jsonl, the CANONICAL one, is merge=union with no such check.
evidence: Measured on master at 6f7846c9, 676 rows: 10 duplicate ids; AT-547/548/549/550/551/552 each hold two rows with DIFFERENT status. ledger/checks.py:141-152 _status_by_id does out[row['id']] = status -- last row in file order wins, unconditionally. Naive dict build over the file: AT-548 open+verified -> reports verified; AT-549 open+verified -> verified; AT-552 open+fixed -> fixed. check_qa_issue_rows (checks.py:155, wired into doctor at doctor.py:265,274) exists specifically because 'AT-401 went back to open a commit after being closed' -- a completeness check built against silent status loss, reading the ledger through the very dict that causes it. SCOPE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: this is a LATENT defeat of that guard, not a currently-firing false clean. 'uv run autotester doctor' reports clean, and correctly so -- all six ids are named in qa/manifests/at540-assertion-layer.md (checked-PASS) but as BARE ids with no parenthetical, so _claims_a_fix (checks.py:108) yields an empty claimed-set and the _passed branch asserts nothing on them. The guard is defeated the moment a manifest uses the documented parenthetical form ('AT-x (low, open -> fixed)', that docstring's own example): the open row is then shadowed by the verified one and the assertion passes on a lie. MEASURED (2026-09-28, the item this row first left open): the session-start hook is ROW-SCANNED and is therefore CORRECT. qa/hooks/mc-sessionstart.ps1:7 counts LINES matching '"status":\s*"(open|Open)"', not a dict by id, so it sees all three shadowed rows. Independent confirmation of the collapse, exact rather than argued: hook line-regex = 183, row-scan = 183, id-dict last-wins = 180. The 3-row discrepancy is precisely AT-548, AT-549 and AT-552 -- the same three derived from the status divergence, reached by a different instrument. The inversion is worth recording: the crude PowerShell line-regex is TRUTHFUL here while the typed Python reader (_status_by_id) is not, because the regex never builds an index and so never has an index to collapse. This NARROWS the row -- no user-facing count is currently wrong. One structural residual in the hook's instrument, not firing today: a per-line count DOUBLE-counts an id whose two rows are both 'open'. Verified no such pair exists on master right now (the 10 pairs are verified+verified, fixed+verified, open+verified x2, fixed+open, open+fixed), so the count is right by luck of the data, not by construction. RESIDUAL SHARPENED (maker, 2026-09-28, accepted): the allocation rule makes this data shape LESS LIKELY BUT NOT FORBIDDEN, and it changes what a future pair looks like. The QUEUE block reservation prevents two writers from drifting into the same id from a shared high-water mark, so a future collision arrives from two writers filing the SAME id concurrently -- and a freshly filed row is almost always 'open'. That is exactly the both-open shape the line count double-counts. So the residual is not 'right by luck of today's data' but 'right by luck of a shape the reservation reduces the frequency of while making it the ONLY shape a new collision can take'. It gets rarer and, when it happens, always hits the double-count. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-28 on 689 rows, and the collapse now has NAMES and a DIRECTION per id. 10 ids appear twice: AT-288/289/290/291 (both rows 'verified', harmless) and AT-547..AT-552, where six of the twelve rows disagree with their twin. By id, first row -> last row: AT-547 fixed->verified; AT-548 OPEN->verified; AT-549 OPEN->verified; AT-550 fixed->verified; AT-551 fixed->OPEN; AT-552 OPEN->fixed. So three ids (AT-548, AT-549, AT-552) carry an `open` row that a last-row-wins read hides, and one (AT-551) goes the other way -- the collapse is not systematically permissive, which is worse than if it were, because a direction-aware reader cannot compensate for it. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOW LIVE ON TWO SURFACES THAT DISAGREE AND NEITHER SAYS SO. qa/hooks/mc-sessionstart.ps1:7 counts LINES (`Get-Content $LEDGER | Where-Object { $_ -match '"status":\s*"(open|Open)"' }`) and prints 'Open issues: 191'. src/autotester/ledger/checks.py:141-152 `_status_by_id` does `out[row['id']] = ...` and so counts 188. Measured both: 191 by every-row, 188 by last-row-wins, and the 3-row gap is exactly AT-548, AT-549, AT-552. The session-start line a human reads is the TRUTHFUL instrument here and the typed code path is the lossy one, which is the reverse of the usual assumption. Nothing reconciles them and nothing reports the divergence: this is C12's pairing row with the pair being two counters, and the defect is the disagreement rather than either count. Open severities today: 19 high, 54 medium, 118 low (by every-row). No new ledger row filed for this -- it is this row's consequence, and a second id for one invariant is how a fix closes on half of itself. THE COST, MEASURED 2026-09-28, AND IT IS WORSE THAN A WRONG STATUS: the two collided pairs are not one issue recorded twice, they are TWO UNRELATED DEFECTS SHARING ONE ID. AT-552 line 549 is Umesh's open 2026-09-06 home-page dashboard ask; AT-552 line 555 is a fixed docstring/exception-suppression defect in assert_expected. AT-551 line 548 is a fixed contextlib.suppress(Exception) in browser/assertions.py::met; AT-551 line 554 is an open UTF-8 BOM + mojibake em-dash in a test file. So an id-keyed read does not merely pick the wrong STATUS -- it returns the WRONG ISSUE, and an instruction to 'fix AT-552' is ambiguous about which defect is meant. This was found by re-deriving a sub-agent's claim that AT-552 is open: it is, on the row the agent happened to read first, and it is not, on the row _status_by_id keeps. The concrete price is on AT-664 -- a verbatim human ask is open, encoded in no criterion, and UNFINDABLE by any id-keyed listing of open work. That is the defect this row predicted, now with a name and a victim, and it raises this row's severity in substance if not in field: a ledger that can lose a human instruction is not a ledger. L8's 'REPORTED, never merged' is the right remedy and it is still unimplemented.
expected: (1) A uniqueness check over qa/issues.jsonl, REPORTED not raised -- the ten existing pairs are HISTORY and must not be destroyed to make a validator green (the maker's own 2026-09-28 finding: renumbering into a range another writer is still advancing cannot converge, qa/QUEUE.md:1333-1363). So: doctor reports each duplicated id as a violation with both line numbers, and the existing pairs are either grandfathered by an explicit allow-list carrying the reason, or remapped once under a manifest -- never silently. (2) _status_by_id must not collapse: an id with two rows returns a state the caller cannot mistake for a single status, so a consumer either handles it or fails, never silently reads the last one. Whichever way it goes, C12(b) applies -- verify by construction: build a ledger with two rows for one id and assert the reader does not report a single clean status. (3) The block reservation in qa/QUEUE.md is the right ALLOCATION rule; it is prose in a queue doc, so it prevents new collisions only while every writer reads it, and does nothing about the pairs already on disk. Criterion home: qa/contracts/living-ledger.md L8.

title: The session-start hook's 'PASS not closed out' detector never checks whether the manifest was flipped. Its own comment claims it finds 'a PASS verdict whose manifest was never flipped to checked-PASS', but the code has no flip check at all: it gates on the SUBSTRING 'Status: ready-for-check' appearing ANYWHERE in the manifest, then counts the unit as unclosed on the verdict alone. STATED FOR THE MANIFEST THAT WILL CLAIM THIS FIX: do not write `1 -> 0` or `count corrected`; the evidence is the SET, not the count, and a capability row resting on the count would pass whether or not the reader was fixed -- AT-697 shape A in a different surface. THE at483 HIT IS REAL, verified here rather than assumed: its verdict carries `**Cycle checked:** 2` and `VERDICT: PASS`, its manifest's last Status field still reads `ready-for-check`, and the fix itself is on master (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 9673f6b HEAD` -> ancestor; `heartbeat` appears 10x in `HEAD:src/autotester/stages/explore_status.py`), so the 2026-09-24 sweep's NOT-ANCESTOR reopening has since been re-landed and the AT-483 row is correctly back to `fixed`. The only thing left undone is the manifest flip to `checked-PASS` -- a dangling handshake of exactly the AT-648 shape, owned by the maker (manifests are not a checker surface), which is why this seat reports it rather than flipping it. ALSO NOTE FOR THE COMING CHECK, unchanged by any of the above: `qa/hooks/*` is an ENFORCEMENT PATH, so this change needs an authorizing `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry carrying `Approved-by: Umesh` BEFORE it lands, and the `scripts/append_decision.ps1` write path is currently classifier-blocked for both seats -- so the code can be finished but cannot legitimately be committed until Umesh either appends the entry himself or grants that path. title: max_actions/max_probes/wall_clock_s = 0 means TWO OPPOSITE things in the two halves of the same gate. During the RUN, stages/parallel_run.py:162 `if approval.max_actions and actions_after > approval.max_actions` treats 0 as falsy and so as UNLIMITED (allow). A signed, unexpired, correctly-scoped approval carrying 0 bounds therefore passes the gate whenever the caller declares actions=0 -- and then enforces nothing at all. core/consent.py:52-62 _shortfalls has NO falsy guard: `if actions > approval.max_actions` -> with max_actions=0, a run declaring actions>=1 is refused (the gate reading: 0 = zero budget). stages/parallel_run.py:153-168 RunBudget.try_consume: `if approval.max_actions and actions_after > approval.max_actions: return False` -> with max_actions=0 the conjunct short-circuits and NO bound is ever applied (the run reading: 0 = unlimited). Same field, opposite meanings, and the permissive one governs what actually happens once a run starts. The reachable path: require_approval's signature is `actions: int = 0, probes: int = 0, wall_clock_s: float = 0.0` (consent.py:100-103), so ANY caller that omits them gets a vacuous gate check -- 0 > 0 is false, _shortfalls returns [], _reject_reason returns None, the approval is returned as covering -- and RunBudget then enforces nothing. CORRECTION BY THE AUTHOR (2026-09-28): this row first claimed 'all three projects/pathlynks/approvals.jsonl rows carry max_actions/max_probes/wall_clock_s = 0, so this is the state on disk today'. That is FALSE for two of the three fields and I withdraw it. Measured: appr_333a83b240ce (max_actions=40, max_probes=0, wall_clock_s=300.0), appr_7ffa35808cf0 (150, 0, 600.0), appr_d89c9e3c61fd (200000, 0, 600000000.0). So only max_probes is 0 on all three; max_actions and wall_clock_s are non-zero on every row. The DEFECT MECHANISM is unaffected and stands verified -- three falsy guards at parallel_run.py:158, :162, :164, and require_approval's 0-defaults at consent.py:100-103 -- but the live-on-disk claim holds for max_probes ONLY, where probes are unlimited today on all three rows. REMEDIATION SCOPE IS ALL THREE GUARDS, NOT ONE -- and this correction is the maker's (2026-09-28), against my own narrowing. I had started to argue that because the UI form carries min='1' on max_actions and wall_clock_s, only max_probes is reachable. That is true of the UI and false of the system. Verified in cli_crawl.py::approve_cmd, the command whose entire job is to SET a bound: :241 max_actions typer.Option(0), :242 max_probes typer.Option(0), :243 wall_clock typer.Option(0.0), and `grep -n 'min='` over the whole file returns NOTHING. So `autotester approve --project X --kind live_case` with no bound flags writes a row that is 0 on every axis, and all three guards at parallel_run.py:158, :162, :164 have a live path into them. Sharper than the asymmetry alone: on approve_cmd every IDENTITY field is required (--kind, --target, --scope, --granted-by, --expires are all typer.Option(...)) while every BOUND defaults to void -- the grant command enforces provenance and not limits. Meanwhile explore_cmd, which RUNS, defaults to max_actions=200 and wall_clock=600.0 (cli_crawl.py:60-61): the bounded command is the one that does not grant. The correct distinction on this row is therefore 'reachable on all three via the CLI; observed on max_probes via the UI' -- NOT 'max_probes only'. A fix scoped to :164 would close one of three inverted guards and read as solved. A SECOND SHAPE the real numbers expose, which the 0-hypothesis hid: appr_d89c9e3c61fd carries wall_clock_s=600000000.0, which is 19.0 YEARS. It is non-zero, so no falsy guard fires and every check passes -- and it constrains nothing. A bound that is present, valid and functionally unlimited is not caught by fixing the 0 semantics at all, and it is the worse failure of the two because it survives a reviewer reading the row. title: qa/issues.jsonl is merge=union with NO id-uniqueness check, while docs/FEATURES.jsonl has normal merge AND two id guards -- the unprotected ledger is the one with 10 documented collisions | MEASURED EXACTLY (maker, 2026-09-28) -- and it is the worse of the two possible shapes. 705 rows, 695 unique ids, 10 duplicated ids, 10 extra rows. In ALL TEN cases the two rows sharing an id are DIFFERENT FINDINGS, not the same finding written twice: AT-288, AT-289, AT-290, AT-291, AT-547, AT-548, AT-549, AT-550, AT-551, AT-552. So the consequence is not redundancy, it is AMBIGUOUS CITATION -- a verdict, manifest or gate that cites "AT-548" does not identify a finding, and there is no way to tell from the citation which of two unrelated defects was meant. Three manifests and the standing checker finding class cite these ids today. The ids fall in exactly two contiguous runs, 288-291 (four) and 547-552 (six), which is the signature of two concurrent block allocations rather than ten independent slips: each event is one session reserving a block that another session had already spent, then both halves surviving the merge because `merge=union` keeps every line and nothing checks ids. The FIX DIRECTION is renumber, never de-duplicate: assign fresh ids to the LATER row of each pair (later by `date`, tie-broken by file order), leave the earlier id pointing where every existing citation already points, and add the id-uniqueness guard that `ledger/store.py:26-27,41` already has for the other ledger so the eleventh collision is refused at write time instead of discovered by a count. TWO WRONG FIXES, recorded so they are not re-proposed: do NOT revert the `merge=union` driver (it is what stops concurrent sessions losing rows outright, which is worse than an ambiguous id), and do NOT delete either row of a pair (both are real findings; deletion destroys one). | CORRECTION AND STRENGTHENING (maker, 2026-09-28, post-merge): the two collisions the at570 merge created were BOTH the dangerous kind, and the one initially called harmless hid it in a field neither seat compared. Measured on `git show e303f5e4:qa/issues.jsonl`: AT-660's two rows had BYTE-EQUAL titles but `evidence` fields of 3902 vs 2520 chars; AT-661's differed in BOTH title (913 vs 665) and evidence (2709 vs 1051). So for the minutes that state was on master, an id-keyed read of AT-660 returned one of two different EVIDENCE texts and of AT-661 one of two different TITLES, depending only on line order. The peer's first pass classified AT-660 as harmless because it compared titles and status and stopped there -- the same shape as every other instrument error today: the comparison reported truthfully about the fields it could reach and was read as a report about the row. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S FIX DIRECTION: a guard that checks id uniqueness at write time is necessary but NOT sufficient, because these rows were not written concurrently -- they were merged. A union merge of a file whose convention is amend-in-place can manufacture a duplicate from two sequential, individually valid writes, and no write-time guard sees a merge. The guard belongs on READ and on MERGE as well as on write: `ledger/store.py`'s duplicate-id check should run when the ledger is loaded, so a merged duplicate fails the next command instead of waiting to be counted. Also recorded, because it nearly stood as the last word: the lossless-resolution check performed on the surviving rows was VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION -- the survivor was built by concatenating both sides, so 'both texts are substrings of the survivor' has one possible answer. Nothing was lost, but that check could not have discovered otherwise, and no side was an annotated superset of the other in 3 of the 4 divergent fields.
evidence: cat .gitattributes -> one line, 'qa/issues.jsonl merge=union'. git check-attr merge: qa/issues.jsonl -> union; docs/FEATURES.jsonl -> unspecified; qa/QUEUE.md -> unspecified. So two branches that each append a row with the SAME id both land in qa/issues.jsonl with no conflict and no warning. Nothing in src/autotester/ validates ids in that file: ledger/checks.py::_status_by_id builds a dict keyed by id, so a duplicate silently resolves to the LAST row read (AT-664's finding, and AT-656's). Meanwhile the OTHER ledger is protected twice over in code that already exists: ledger/store.py:26-27 raises ValueError '<path>:<n>: duplicate id (rows are append-only)' when loading, and :41 raises '<id> already exists in <path>' on add.
expected: Name the structural cause on the incident family instead of filing an 11th instance of it. Ten duplicate ids in qa/issues.jsonl have each been recorded as a numbering mistake by whoever made it (including two by this maker: the AT-654->AT-656 renumber, and the reservation-table wording that sent the peer checker to a spent AT-670). They are not ten mistakes. They are one missing guard plus a merge driver chosen to avoid conflicts, and union merge is exactly what removes the signal a colliding append would otherwise produce. The fix is NOT to change the merge driver: union is why two sessions can append concurrently at all, and reverting it trades silent duplicates for constant conflicts on the busiest file in the repo. The fix is the guard that FEATURES.jsonl already has -- load-time id-uniqueness validation over qa/issues.jsonl, so a duplicate is refused at the next read rather than resolved silently by a dict. Do NOT pair this with de-duplicating the existing rows: AT-656 and AT-664 show the collapse is not consistently permissive (AT-548/549/552 hide an open row, AT-551 goes the other way), so rewriting history here changes statuses. New guard, existing rows left alone and their collisions recorded.

title: Running a verify command through a pipe silently discards BOTH its exit code and its diagnostics, so a failing suite reports success to whoever is judging. `uv run pytest 2>&1 | tail -15` over master returned exit 0 while pytest had `1 failed`; the harness printed `[exited with code 0]` and a checker reading only that line would have recorded a green baseline. This is not a pytest defect and not fixable in src/ -- it is a defect in how this project's own maker and checker RUN their verify commands, and both roles do it.
evidence: Measured directly, three ways in one shell: `false | tail -1; echo $?` -> 0. `set -o pipefail; false | tail -1; echo $?` -> 1. `bash -c 'exit 3'; echo $?` -> 3. POSIX defines a pipeline's status as the LAST command's, so `tail` (which succeeds at tailing a failing run) is what the caller sees. Live instance the same day: `uv run pytest 2>&1 | tail -15` in this session reported `[exited with code 0]` while its own summary line read `1 failed, 2150 passed, 6 skipped, 14 xfailed, 15 warnings in 2241.34s` (tests/test_flake_probe_real_process.py, AT-518). The second loss is worse than the exit code and has no workaround once taken: `tail -15` kept the summary and threw away the traceback, so the occurrence could not be matched against AT-518's recorded FileNotFoundError shape at all and had to be filed as cause-unknown. AT-518's own evidence field already states the correct practice -- 'output to a file, scanned whole per AT-503/this project's own standing rule -- never a tail' -- which means this rule was known, written down inside the ledger, and still not followed by the next checker to run the suite, including me.
expected: Not a code fix. Two mechanical ones, both cheap: (1) any verify command whose result is judged must redirect to a file (`uv run pytest > .work/<name>.txt 2>&1; echo exit=$?`) and be read from the file, never piped to head/tail/grep/wc for the purpose of deciding pass/fail -- filtering a file you have kept is fine, filtering a stream you did not is not; (2) `set -o pipefail` in any script that pipes a command whose status matters. The durable form belongs in qa/contracts/core-invariants.md as a C12 row rather than in src/: C12 already says every signal must fail closed and that the variable is whether the instrument has any REPRESENTATION for the thing it must tell apart -- a pipe has no representation for a non-zero exit and none for a line it dropped, so it fails OPEN in both directions at once, toward a false green and toward an undiagnosable failure. Filed high, above AT-518 which it obscured, because it is the shape that can turn a FAIL into a PASS in a verdict, and PASS is the one thing only this role can grant. The C12 amendment is the checker's to write and is deliberately NOT written in this pass -- the row comes first so the reasoning is on the ledger before the rule, and the rule should name the maker's practice too, which means it wants the maker's confirmation that the same rule binds it.
source: Mode B sweep follow-through 2026-09-28: found while establishing an independent pytest baseline, i.e. found by the instrument failing on the checker's own work, not by inspecting anyone else's
