title: `uv run pytest` is the first of three gate commands in qa/adapter.json carrying `"expect": "exit 0"`, and in BOTH whole-suite runs measured on 2026-09-28 it exited 1 -- on a single load-dependent failure (AT-518) that passes 3/3 in isolation and is unrelated to any unit. While that holds, the gate's literal pass condition is unmet for every unit, so each checker must decide BY HAND that the red belongs to the machine and not to the work it is judging. That is the C12 shape on the gate itself: the command has no representation for 'failed for a reason that is not this unit's', so it collapses either into a false red blocking every unit or into a habit of excusing reds -- and the second is the reachable one, because a checker who excuses a red twice will excuse the third without reading it. | FOURTH LOADED OCCURRENCE, REPORTED BY THE PEER AND NOT MEASURED BY ME -- recorded as its evidence, attributed, because it moves n and I did not run it: the at570 build agent's own whole-suite run gave `1 failed, 2166 passed, 6 skipped, 14 xfailed`, exit 1, 1698s, the same AT-518 signature, with an immediate isolated re-run at `2 passed in 15.81s`. (2166 rather than my 2150 is consistent with that worktree carrying the unit's new 268-line tests/test_ui_runs_live_case_approval.py.) So the loaded side is now 4 occurrences and the isolated side 4 passes -- BUT this run sat under its own build load, so it reproduces the confound rather than separating it and moves n ONLY on the loaded side. The idle run that would separate it has still not happened: the peer declined to run one under the at570 checker's load rather than run a confounded suite and call it clean, which is the right call and is why this row's rate claim stays unestablished. Nothing here changes the severity or the recommendation. | RATE CLAIM CLOSED AS UNESTABLISHED-WITH-REASON (maker, 2026-09-28), on the peer's framing: "an unestablished rate stated as unestablished is a finishable state; an owed measurement that keeps not happening is the thing AT-641 is about." The idle whole-suite baseline that would separate load from defect was owed for four ticks and never taken, because every slot since filing had a live build or a live checker holding the RAM ceiling at 0 (ceiling = floor((free RAM - 2GB)/~0.6GB); measured 2.52 then 2.47 GB free). All four loaded occurrences are therefore confounded and all four isolated re-runs passed, so the honest statement is: THE RATE UNDER IDLE CONDITIONS IS NOT MEASURED, and no number should be quoted for it. Continuing to carry it as owed was itself becoming the AT-641 defect -- a measurement deferred indefinitely reads, in every report, exactly like a measurement that came back clean. RECLAIMABLE, not closed: the first tick with a genuinely idle slot runs `uv run pytest` whole-suite with no subagent dispatched, and this clause is replaced by the number. What is NOT affected: the severity stays high and the recommendation is unchanged, because the gate defect does not depend on the rate -- `expect: exit 0` has no representation for "failed for a reason that is not this unit's" whether that happens 1 run in 4 or every run. | THE ROW'S OWN PREDICTION CAME TRUE AGAINST ITS AUTHOR, 2026-09-28, and this is the strongest evidence in the row because it demonstrates the mechanism instead of forecasting it. Before at570's post-merge suite had reported ANYTHING, I told the maker that if it came back red on `test_run_once_kills_a_real_hung_child` 'that is the known AT-518 flake and not the merge.' That is a verdict on a failure nobody had read yet, offered by the seat whose entire function is that reds get read, and it is verbatim option (c) of this row's own `expected` field -- 'leave it and let every checker excuse the red by hand -- today's state, and the one that quietly destroys the gate' -- performed by the person who wrote option (c), one turn after writing it. It is also the thing this row's title warns about in a sentence I wrote: 'a checker who excuses a red twice will excuse the third without reading it.' I did not need two; I needed zero, because the excuse was available as a ready-made explanation and the explanation is probably even TRUE. That is what makes this class dangerous rather than merely sloppy: a pre-excuse is not wrong often enough to be self-correcting. AGGRAVATING RATHER THAN MITIGATING, the maker's point and it is right: a pre-excuse offered by the OTHER seat is more persuasive than one the maker would give itself, because it arrives with the authority of the seat that is supposed to withhold it. The gate does not fail when a maker wants to ship; it fails when the checker hands it a reason. The maker refused it, which is the second time today the pair's value came from the OTHER seat declining something offered in good faith. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROW: the loaded-side count stays at 4 and this is NOT a fifth occurrence -- no run had reported when I said it, so there is nothing to count; what changed is that the erosion mechanism moved from predicted to observed, which is a reason the severity is high and not a reason to raise n. The protocol the maker will use instead is recorded here because it is better than what this seat offered and should be the standing procedure for any red attributed to a known flake: read the failure text, confirm the signature MATCHES AT-518 rather than assuming it, re-run the failing test in isolation, and check the failing module's import graph against the merge's changed paths. The fourth is the one that does the real work -- a signature match cannot distinguish 'the flake fired again' from 'the merge broke the same test', and only the import graph can say whether the changed paths could reach that module at all. I could not have supplied any of the four from where I was standing, which is the whole objection to what I said. | WHAT THAT LAPSE ACTUALLY PROVES, and it strengthens this row's RECOMMENDATION rather than merely embarrassing its author (the maker's inference, 2026-09-28, and it is sharper than the one I drew from my own mistake): option (c) does not fail from a LACK of discipline, it fails UNDER discipline. The person who performed it had written the warning against it into this very field one turn earlier, was holding the row in context, and had spent the day filing instrument errors against both seats. If those conditions are not enough, then 'leave it and let every checker excuse the red by hand' is not an option whose viability depends on checkers being careful -- it is an option that is unavailable to careful checkers too, because the thing it asks for is not care but the absence of a ready-made explanation, and this gate supplies one every time it fires. STATED AT ITS ACTUAL STRENGTH, because n=1 and this row's own last clause forbids reading a rate off one trial: this is NOT evidence about how often a checker excuses a red. It is a single counterexample, and what it refutes is a UNIVERSAL -- the claim that (c) is safe provided checkers read each red before excusing it. One instance is logically sufficient against a universal and logically worthless as a frequency, and the distinction is the whole reason it belongs in the argument rather than in the count (the loaded side stays at 4 for exactly the same reason). CONSEQUENCE: the recommendation of (a) -- fix `test_run_once_kills_a_real_hung_child` -- now rests on more than a preference for green suites, and (b) `xfail` with a named expiry is now the weaker fallback rather than a near-equal one, because (b) still routes every future red through a human's judgement about whether THIS red is the expected one and that is the judgement just shown to fail while held by someone who had written the warning. (c) should be read as ruled out rather than merely discouraged. Umesh's call either way -- it is still a src/ change and still his decision, and this only changes the strength of the case, not who makes it. ALSO RECORDED, the cold-read protocol both seats agreed for when the post-merge suite lands: the maker sends the checker the failure TEXT ONLY -- no test name framing, no attribution, no mention of AT-518 -- and asks what it is. Its reason is the correct one and is the reason it is written here: a conclusion sent alongside the evidence turns the second reader into a reviewer of the first reader's work, which is not an independent read, and both seats did exactly that to each other twice on 2026-09-28. | OPTION (a) IS NOW SPECIFIED RATHER THAN NAMED, 2026-09-28, from the cold read of the failure this row's gate kept excusing (AT-700). 'Fix the test' does NOT mean de-flake it: the test conflates 'my scenario never started' with 'the tree kill is broken', and both surface as the same `FileNotFoundError`. The fix is to poll for `child.pid` with a bounded wait before the timed call and treat its absence as a scenario-did-not-start ERROR, so that `assert not _alive(...)` is only ever a statement about run_once. This also settles (b) for good: `xfail` silences BOTH states at once, including the state where the tree kill has genuinely been removed -- the exact mutation that test's docstring says it is the only guard against -- so (b) is no longer a weaker fallback, it is unavailable. The remaining choice for Umesh is (a) as specified above, and the ranking (a) > (b) > (c) collapses to (a) alone. Also note what the cold read cost and bought: with the 'known AT-518 flake' label attached, this would have been counted as a fifth occurrence and excused; without it, the failing assertion turned out not to be the one the test is named for. | FIXED VIA OPTION (a), AND THE JUSTIFICATION IS THE MECHANISM, NOT THE GREEN RUN. 2026-09-28: the first whole-suite run after at700-setup-vs-subject cycle 2 (PASS, 726074d5) is `2167 passed, 6 skipped, 14 xfailed, 15 warnings in 2137.99s (0:35:37)`, EXIT 0, run by this seat unpiped per AT-692. That is the gate's literal `expect: exit 0` met for the first time in any measured run. BUT ONE GREEN SUITE IS NOT WHY THIS ROW CLOSES, and this repo ships the instrument that says so: `scripts/flake_probe.ceiling_given_no_failures(1)` -> 95.0%, i.e. a single clean run bounds the true failure rate at ninety-five percent, which is no evidence whatsoever. Seeing a 1-in-14 flake with 95% confidence needs 41 runs = 24.3 hours of wall clock at this suite's length. Closing on the run alone would have been AT-335's exact error with a smaller sample. WHAT DOES JUSTIFY IT is that AT-518's cause was measured and removed rather than out-waited: the scenario file moved inside the repo, dropping the nested run's collect cost from 19.68s (from system temp, 14,645 entries) to 0.64s, against a 20s bound -- roughly 8x margin where there was previously a bound BELOW the floor. RESIDUAL, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: exit 0 is not structurally guaranteed. Under enough contention the scenario can still fail to start within 20s and the test still FAILS (`pytest.fail`, never a skip -- a skip here is the silencing this row objected to). What changed is that the red now CARRIES ITS OWN ATTRIBUTION: `scenario never started ... This says NOTHING about run_once's tree kill, passing or broken`, at :119, distinct in line, exception type and message from the subject's red at :125. That is precisely what this row asked for -- its complaint was C12-shaped, that the command `has no representation for 'failed for a reason that is not this unit's'`. It has one now. The checker no longer decides by hand; the failure states which it is.
evidence: qa/adapter.json `verify.commands[0] = {"cmd": "uv run pytest", "expect": "exit 0"}`, read verbatim. Both runs on master at e154e0df with no source change between them: `1 failed, 2150 passed, 6 skipped, 14 xfailed, 15 warnings in 2241.34s (0:37:21)` and `... in 1533.85s (0:25:33)`, identical sole failure (tests/test_flake_probe_real_process.py::test_run_once_kills_a_real_hung_process_and_its_real_grandchild). Run 2 was redirected rather than piped, so its status was observable: `echo exit=$?` -> `exit=1`. Isolation control, 3 consecutive runs of that file alone: exit 0, `2 passed`. Traceback kept at .work/pytest-baseline-2026-09-28.txt:32-92 (FileNotFoundError on the child pid file). SCOPE OF THE CLAIM, STATED SO IT IS NOT OVERREAD: this is n=2 on the whole-suite side. It does NOT establish a rate, and it does not establish that the gate can never return 0 -- an earlier draft of this row said 'CANNOT return exit 0' and that was withdrawn before filing. Both whole-suite runs also ran while the peer's at570 build agent held a subagent slot on a machine measured at 2.52 GB free RAM, a confound I cannot separate from suite size with this data. SECOND LIVE INSTANCE OF AT-692 IN THE SAME MEASUREMENT, and the reason it is recorded here: the background task's own trailing `tail -6` made the harness print `[exited with code 0]` for a command whose captured status was 1. A checker reading the harness line rather than the kept file would have recorded this suite as green on two different days.
expected: A decision for Umesh, as options, because each carries a cost the others do not. (a) Make the test independent of machine contention -- the honest fix, the only one that restores the gate's literal meaning, the maker's to do in tests/, and AT-196/AT-505 suggest the shape generalises past this one test. (b) `xfail(strict=False)` or quarantine into a separately-run group: restores exit 0 immediately and is cheapest, but converts a real reproducible failure into a permanently silenced one, and silencing a signal is the exact failure this project judges other software for. (c) Leave it and let every checker excuse the red by hand -- today's state, and the one that quietly destroys the gate. I recommend (a), and would accept (b) ONLY with a named expiry and a ledger row, never open-ended. What I will not do is weaken a criterion to accommodate it: until it is fixed, a verdict in this repo must state that `uv run pytest` exited 1, cite this row, and show the sole failure is outside the unit's changed paths -- a judgement a checker makes and records, which is not something the adapter can assert. Worth measuring before deciding, and cheap: one whole-suite run with no build agent holding a slot would separate the confound named above. Not filed against any unit and no fix cycle charged -- no unit caused this.

title: `qa/hooks/mc-sessionstart.ps1:11-12` enumerates `qa/manifests` relative to the CURRENT checkout only, and the string 'worktree' appears in the file zero times. The maker-checker handshake is FILES, and this is the request half of that handshake being unreadable by anyone except the session that wrote it.
evidence: Measured against the live tree, not reconstructed. `git ls-files qa/manifests/ | grep -i 570` -> nothing; `ls qa/manifests/at570*` -> No such file. The manifest exists only at .claude/worktrees/agent-ac0c11769db9a7239/qa/manifests/at570-live-case-approval.md, carrying `**Fix cycle:** 1 of max 3` at :22 and `## Status: ready-for-check` at :424, committed in e7bfeb6b at 2026-09-28T04:40:48+05:30. Note what this is NOT: it is not the eight-spellings problem (AT-662) -- `## Status: ready-for-check` would match the hook's substring pattern at :13 perfectly well if the file were in the enumerated directory. expected: THE REASON THIS IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A NOTE: the same hook is now measured failing in BOTH directions from the same run. It reports `PASS not closed out: 1` for t182, whose matched phrase is PROSE explaining the handshake (AT-673, a false positive, fails toward alarm), and in the same line reports `Checks pending: 0` for at570, which genuinely is pending (a false negative, fails toward silence). That is the maker's AT-668/AT-669 insight -- one hook, opposite directions, one root -- and it now has a second confirmed instance in a different predicate, which strengthens rather than repeats the 'a partial fix is worse than none' gate: fixing only the alarm side would leave a hook that is silent exactly when a maker dies. Today the loop still works because the maker dispatches its own checker subagent straight at the worktree, so the invisible state has a live owner; it becomes unrecoverable in precisely the scenario AT-641 already documented happening once, where the session holding the knowledge died mid-unit. The fix is a gate decision for Umesh, not mine to make and not mine to write: `qa/hooks/*` is an enforcement path needing `Approved-by: Umesh` (Lab Protocol), and AT-668 says that guard does not even cover `qa/hooks/*` today. Direction only, for that conversation: enumerate `git worktree list --porcelain` and scan each tree's `qa/manifests`, which is the same enumeration AT-643 asks for, so one change answers both. title: `doctor.py::check_generated_fresh` (L1, 'ARCHITECTURE generated sections and SNAPSHOT must equal a fresh regeneration') compares the file ON DISK against a fresh render and never consults git, so a generated file that is current in the working tree but STALE IN THE COMMITTED BLOB passes clean. The repo is then stale for everyone who clones it while `doctor: clean` is true on the one machine holding the uncommitted regeneration. Measured live today: master at 82677b26 had `docs/SNAPSHOT.md` modified-uncommitted, `doctor` reported clean, and `git show 82677b26:docs/SNAPSHOT.md | grep -c F-065` -> 0 against 2 in the working tree. A fresh clone of that commit would have FAILED L1. | TWO CONSTRAINTS ON ANY FIX, THE FIRST A CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN A DETAIL (the peer's finding, re-derived here, 2026-09-28). (1) LINE-ENDING NORMALISATION IS MANDATORY. `git config --show-scope --get-all core.autocrlf` -> `system  true`, so the committed blob stores LF while the working tree holds CRLF. Measured on docs/SNAPSHOT.md: disk CRLF=44 bare-LF=0; `git show HEAD:docs/SNAPSHOT.md` CRLF=0 bare-LF=44; raw bytes equal -> False; equal after LF-normalisation -> True. So the natural blob-vs-disk comparison reports EVERY generated file as uncommitted on EVERY run on this machine -- which is this row's own defect class reproduced inside its fix: an instrument reporting confidently about something other than what its name claims. (2) THE FALSIFICATION CONDITION, AND THE PEER'S REASON FOR IT WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT MATTERS. It said a green suite is no evidence because a fixture built with `git init` in a tmpdir 'may not inherit this machine's autocrlf'. Measured: it DOES inherit it -- autocrlf is set at SYSTEM scope, so `git -C <tmpdir> init` then `config --get core.autocrlf` -> true. The fixture still compares equal, for a different reason: normalisation only manifests when git WRITES the file out. A fixture that writes a file with LF and commits it leaves LF on disk (probe: disk CRLF=0, blob CRLF=0, raw equal True), and git even warns 'LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it'. After forcing that touch -- `rm gen.md; git checkout -- gen.md` -- the same fixture reads disk CRLF=3, blob CRLF=0, raw equal False, LF-normalised equal True. SO THE PRESCRIPTION IS PRECISE: a test proves nothing unless its fixture CHECKS THE FILE OUT (clone, `git checkout --`, or delete-and-restore) after committing it; write-then-commit passes whether or not the implementation normalises. The peer's conclusion (a green suite is not evidence) stands; its mechanism (inheritance) does not, and the difference is the whole test. (3) SITING, unresolved and deliberately not resolved by either of us: `doctor.py` 279/300 (headroom 21), `core/paths.py` 287/300, `ledger/render.py` 300/300, `tests/test_doctor.py` 300/300 -- the check is ~25-30 lines and its tests need their own module, so the only routes are compacting doctor.py's near-duplicate MAP/SNAPSHOT blocks or a new module, and the anti-drift rule reserves both for the human. The peer recommends the refactor and I agree it needs a checker on it specifically, because the two branches are NOT symmetric: the MAP branch catches `ValueError` (doctor.py:206) while the SNAPSHOT branch catches `Exception` and EARLY-RETURNS (:212, :215), so 'behaviour-preserving' is precisely the claim to falsify rather than assert -- a compaction that unifies them silently changes which failures are swallowed and whether later violations are still collected. | FIXTURE SHAPE C ADDED AND VERIFIED, 2026-09-28 (the peer's, re-derived here): a fresh `git clone` triggers the same write-out as a checkout, so it reproduces the asymmetry. Probe in a throwaway repo -- shape A (write LF, commit): disk CRLF=0, blob CRLF=0, raw equal TRUE; shape C (clone of that repo): disk CRLF=3, blob CRLF=0, raw equal FALSE, LF-normalised equal TRUE. So there are three acceptable fixture shapes and A is NOT one of them: B `rm` + `git checkout --`, C a fresh clone, or any other route that makes git WRITE the file out. C is the one to prefer, because a clone is the scenario this row is ABOUT -- the stale repo everyone else gets -- so the fixture and the defect's own story become one construction, which is C12's rule that the construction has to be the one the claim is about. A shape-A fixture is a finding in its own right, not merely a weak test: it passes whether or not the implementation normalises. AND THE PLAINEST INSTANCE OF THE DAY, the peer's observation: git PRINTS this trap on every commit -- `warning: in the working copy of '<file>', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it` -- the whole defect lives in that 'next time', and the warning sat in both sessions' scrollback all day, including in the tool output of the very probe that measured it. An instrument reporting correctly to nobody.
evidence: src/autotester/doctor.py::check_generated_fresh reads `docs.snapshot.read_text(encoding='utf-8')` and compares it to `render_snapshot(docs)`, both resolved from RepoDocs paths on disk; `grep -c 'git\|subprocess' src/autotester/doctor.py` -> 1, and no git object is ever read. Live instance, all four commands at the same instant: `git status --short docs/SNAPSHOT.md` -> ' M docs/SNAPSHOT.md'; `uv run autotester doctor` -> exit 0 'doctor: clean'; `grep -c F-065 docs/SNAPSHOT.md` -> 2; `git show 82677b26:docs/SNAPSHOT.md | grep -c F-065` -> 0. The peer has since committed the regeneration (49bed42e, 'commit the SNAPSHOT regeneration that was masking master's staleness'), after which `git show HEAD:docs/SNAPSHOT.md | grep -c F-065` -> 2 and the tree is clean -- so the defect is currently unexpressed, which is exactly why it is worth a row: nothing in the check prevents it recurring the next time a generated file is regenerated and not committed. This is the C12 shape with the two sites being one file's two OBJECTS: the instrument was honest about what it read, and what it read was not what anyone thought they were asking about.
expected: A doctor check rather than a hook, per the peer's own preference and I agree -- a hook would only fire on commit, while the failure is a state the repo can sit in. Direction: for each generated artifact (docs/MAP.md, docs/SNAPSHOT.md), L1 should additionally compare the COMMITTED blob against the fresh render, or more simply assert the artifact is not modified-uncommitted while also matching the render, so that `doctor: clean` means committed == disk == fresh regeneration. That last sentence is the peer's and it is the right definition. It is a src/ change and therefore the maker's; proposed, not built. Worth stating what it does NOT need: no new generated artifact, no schema change, and no enforcement path -- doctor is already the declared validator in CLAUDE.md's design-rules section, so this widens an existing check rather than adding a gate.

title: After at570 lands, EVERY UI case run (`POST /projects/{slug}/run`) is refused until a signed `live_case` `RunApproval` exists -- and the UI has no way to create one. `ui/routes_crawl_approval.py` hard-codes `run_kind=ApprovalKind.CRAWL` on the row it writes (:188) and filters the approvals table to `ApprovalKind.CRAWL` (:104), so the only grant path for a case run is `uv run autotester approve --kind live_case` on the CLI. F-042 shipped 'complete no-CLI crawl approval' and ui.md U11 requires an operator to authorize a crawl without the CLI; the same operator can no longer start a RUN without it. Not a reason to reopen the fail-open -- fail-closed is correct and consent.md's out-of-scope list explicitly excludes a UI grant form -- but the consequence is a shipped product state, not a field-level gap, and the at570 manifest discloses only the narrower `max_probes` field absence (D2/AT-675) and 'the CLI is the intended path' (D4).
evidence: `grep -n 'run_kind=ApprovalKind' src/autotester/ui/routes_crawl_approval.py` -> :188 `run_kind=ApprovalKind.CRAWL` (the only kind the form can write); :104 `crawl = [a for a in approvals if a.run_kind is ApprovalKind.CRAWL]` (the only kind the table lists, so a CLI-granted live_case row is also invisible in the UI). `src/autotester/ui/routes_runs.py::_require_live_case_approval` asks `covering_approval(..., kind=ApprovalKind.LIVE_CASE)`, and all three rows in projects/pathlynks/approvals.jsonl are run_kind=crawl. Verified in the at570 worktree at a169d45a by the checker, not taken from the manifest. The refusal itself IS readable: `ui/error_pages.py` (AT-596) renders HTTPException as a themed HTML page for a browser and carries `require_approval`'s grant command verbatim -- so the operator is told exactly what to type, in the UI, and the thing they are told to type is a terminal command.
expected: Widen the existing approval form to choose the kind (at minimum CRAWL | LIVE_CASE) and list every kind in the approvals table, in the same unit as AT-675's missing `max_probes` field -- one pass over `routes_crawl_approval.py` closes both. Until then the state is honest and documented rather than hidden. Deliberately NOT proposed: a UI-side default-grant, an auto-grant, or any relaxation of the gate.

The build agent was right that a UI grant form is out of consent.md's scope; the finding is that the operator-facing consequence of correctly closing the fail-open was under-disclosed, which is a manifest completeness point and not a defect in the fix.

title: The SERIAL case-run path (the DEFAULT, plan.n<=1) is gated at preflight but has no mid-run budget at all. AT-570 puts `_require_live_case_approval` in front of every UI case run, so a serial run cannot START without a signed live_case approval -- but `ui/run_execution.py::_run_cases_serially` never constructs a `RunBudget` and never calls `try_consume`, so once it starts, the approval's max_actions / max_probes / wall_clock_s bound nothing. Only the parallel path (`stages/parallel_run.py::run_cases`) enforces them.
evidence: ui/run_execution.py::_run_cases_serially takes no `approval` parameter and its body contains no RunBudget reference; it loops `for case in normal_cases: _run_and_grade_resilient(...)` on one shared BrowserSession. ui/routes_runs.py::trigger_run calls `_require_live_case_approval` BEFORE branching, so the GATE covers serial; only the RUN side differs. Stated precisely: a serial run declares actions=sum(action_cost) and wall_clock=that x 8.0 at the gate and is refused if the approval is narrower, so an over-budget serial run never starts -- but a serial run that starts and then overruns is not stopped mid-run. The asymmetry is invisible to a reader of routes_runs.py, which shows one preflight for both paths.
expected: Either thread the approval into `_run_cases_serially` and check `budget.try_consume(actions=action_cost(case))` per case exactly as `stages/parallel_run.py::_run_one` does (the cheap fix, and it makes the two paths say the same thing), or state in `_run_cases_serially`'s docstring that its bound is preflight-only and why that is sufficient. Not done in at570 because threading a budget through the serial loop changes a path carrying its own three live regressions (AT-574/AT-576/AT-577) and this unit's scope was the fail-open default, not serial parity. Disclosed in qa/manifests/at570-live-case-approval.md.

title: `WALL_CLOCK_PER_ACTION_S = 8.0` in stages/run_budget.py duplicates browser/session.py's own 8000 ms settle ceiling by hand, because session.py is AT the 300-line design cap and cannot take an exported constant. Two copies of one number, and the copy that would go stale is the consent-sizing one.
evidence: browser/session.py:237 uses an 8000 ms settle ceiling; src/autotester/stages/run_budget.py defines WALL_CLOCK_PER_ACTION_S = 8.0 with a docstring citing that line. `wc -l src/autotester/browser/session.py` = 300 exactly, so adding an exported module constant to it would put it over doctor's file-too-long rule in the same commit. Nothing links the two: changing the settle ceiling will not change the consent request size, and no test asserts they agree.
expected: When browser/session.py is next split for length, export the settle ceiling from it and import it in run_budget.py, with a test asserting WALL_CLOCK_PER_ACTION_S == that ceiling / 1000. Until then this is a knowingly-duplicated constant, not an oversight -- C3 (one concept, one place) is violated and the reason is a design cap in another file.
source: at570-live-case-approval: sizing the wall clock a case run asks the gate for

title: CN10 asks that an implausible bound be VISIBLE to a human rather than capped. at570 records `Run.bounds` (schema/run.py::RunBounds: approval_id plus the three bounds) into run.json for every UI case run -- but nothing renders it. The 19-year wall clock on the live pathlynks approval therefore lands in a JSON file a human has to open by hand, not on the run page or in the report.

Grepping 'bounds' across src/autotester/ui returns only crawl-bounds form/parse code and routes_runs' own write -- no read and no render in routes_report.py or any view module. `wc -l src/autotester/ui/routes_report.py` = 300 exactly, i.e. AT the design cap, so a bounds card cannot be added to it without splitting it first. stages/report_export.py (Excel/HTML export) does not read Run.bounds either.

title: The command whose job is to SET a bound defaults to UNBOUNDED, while the command it bounds defaults to BOUNDED. `autotester approve` defaults max_actions=0, max_probes=0, wall_clock=0.0 with no min= on any of them; `autotester crawl` defaults max_actions=200, wall_clock=600.0. So `approve --project X --kind live_case` with no bound flags writes a row that is zero on every axis -- which, under the pre-AT-660 falsy guards, then ran UNBOUNDED on every axis. The disk evidence is narrower than the defect and was twice read as making it harmless. | STALE MECHANISM, CORRECTED BY THE CHECKER 2026-09-28 (appended, not edited -- the row's original text stands as history). This row's framing rests on `0` meaning UNBOUNDED. It no longer does anywhere in this codebase, and it has not since AT-660/CN10 landed -- a row this seat verified and which is `status: verified` on the ledger. Re-derived here from the source rather than from that row: `core/consent.py::_shortfalls:56-59` compares `actions > approval.max_actions` plainly; `stages/run_budget.py::try_consume:64-71` does the same and additionally returns False on `approval.wall_clock_s <= 0`; its class docstring `:36-41` states the change in terms -- *'every bound means the same thing here as it does at the gate, namely that ZERO GRANTS NOTHING. The truthiness guards this replaces (`if approval.max_actions and ...`) made `0` mean unlimited during the run while the gate read the same `0` as a zero budget'*; and `schema/approval.py:56-75` now carries `ZERO MEANS ZERO` in the description of all three fields. The falsy guard at `parallel_run.py:164` that these rows cite is GONE -- that line is now `budget.try_consume(...)`, delegating to `RunBudget`. SPECIFIC TO THIS ROW: the title's claim -- *the command whose job is to SET a bound defaults to UNBOUNDED* -- is FALSE against current code. `cli_crawl.py:241-243` does still default all three bounds to `0` with no `min=1`, which remains a real defect, but a grant typed without flags now writes an approval that authorises NOTHING: every run against it is refused at `_shortfalls`. The accurate statement is the inverse and is still worth fixing: *the command whose job is to set a bound defaults to a grant that can never cover any run*, so the CLI's default output is a dead approval rather than an open one. This also settles the security question on the pending `0 -> 200/600 with min=1` edit, which a harness classifier refused as [Security Weaken] on 2026-09-28: raising those defaults does not weaken any enforced boundary, because the boundary is the account's own rights (D-056 direction) and the bound is a runaway brake; what it changes is a command that by default emits an unusable grant into one that emits a working bounded one, with `min=1` making the void shape unreachable.
evidence: cli_crawl.py:241 `max_actions: int = typer.Option(0, "--max-actions")`; :242 `max_probes: int = typer.Option(0, "--max-probes")`; :243 `wall_clock: float = typer.Option(0.0, "--wall-clock")` -- these are `approve`, the GRANTING command, and none carries a min=. cli_crawl.py:60-61 `max_actions: int = typer.Option(200, ...)`, `wall_clock: float = typer.Option(600.0, ...)` -- these are `crawl`, the command that RUNS under those bounds. The UI grant form is the opposite of the CLI: routes_crawl_approval.py:178 raises 'crawl approval bounds must be positive' and the form carries min='1' on the two fields it has, which is why all three rows on disk are non-zero on max_actions and wall_clock_s, and why 'AT-660 is live on max_probes only' reads as true of the DISK and is false of the CODE. AT-660's 0-semantics fix (this branch) closes the consequence; the default itself is untouched.
expected: Give `approve`'s three bound options no default at all (required flags) or a deliberately small one, so a grant cannot be silently unbounded, and add min= validation matching the UI's. NOT changed in at570: altering a granting command's defaults changes what every existing script and doc line produces, which is its own blast radius and its own gate. Filed here because it is the cleanest single statement of the fail-open class this wave is about -- and because it is the reason 'the bounds default to 0, so a bad row is harmless' was wrong twice.

title: The qa/QUEUE.md id reservation gives AT-690..AT-709 to 'the checker' -- a ROLE, not a session -- and there are two entities holding that role at once: this standing checker seat and the fresh checker subagent the maker dispatches per unit. That subagent filed AT-698 from inside the reserved block while this seat was about to use the same id. Caught before landing by a pre-append `assert id not in ids` guard, so no eleventh duplicate exists; nothing in the ledger or the reservation table would have caught it, which is AT-656/AT-676 exactly -- union merge, no id guard in the file, and a reservation that cannot express two holders. | TWO MEASURED EXTENSIONS, 2026-09-28, both from the at570 merge landing while this row was being written. (1) THE MERGE'S OWN COLLISIONS WERE DIVERGENT, NOT IDENTICAL, which is the dangerous sub-class rather than the harmless one. `git show e303f5e4:qa/issues.jsonl` carried AT-660 twice and AT-661 twice. AT-660's two titles were byte-equal (the differing field was `status`), but AT-661's were NOT: 913 chars against 665, divergent rather than one being a prefix of the other -- so for a few minutes an id-keyed read of AT-661 returned one of two different issues depending on line order, which is AT-656's failure mode arriving by merge instead of by two writers. The peer's resolution is VERIFIED LOSSLESS by this seat and that is worth stating because I had argued against pairing a guard with de-duplication: both merge versions' titles are fully contained in the surviving row (2180 chars) and both their `evidence` fields (2709 and 1051 chars) are contained in the surviving 4362-char one, checked by substring rather than by eye. So the de-duplication I warned about turned out safe HERE; the warning stands for rows whose divergence is real rather than additive, and this one was additive because the longer side was an annotated superset. (2) C10's PATH DISCIPLINE DOES NOT COVER A CO-EDITED FILE, and this seat is the one it happened to: the peer's close-out commit ea8a52b2 contains THIS row and AT-709, which were written to the working tree by the checker and never committed by it. `git commit --only -- qa/issues.jsonl` is C10-compliant by the letter, since it names its path and touches nothing else -- but naming a path protects against sweeping up UNRELATED files, not against sweeping up another session's uncommitted edits to the SAME file. The consequence is small here (the rows landed intact, under the wrong commit message, so the reasoning that belonged in a checker commit message exists only in the rows themselves) and would not be small for a half-written edit: a script that appends two rows is briefly a file with one. Both seats append to this one file all day, so the durable form is either `git stash`-free discipline (never leave the ledger dirty across a turn -- commit each append immediately, which this seat had not done) or a real id/append guard per AT-676. Reported, not fixed: C10 lives in the maker's and the project's own commit discipline, not on a checker surface. | CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN DIVERGENCE TABLE, 2026-09-28, appended not edited (the peer's measurement, re-derived here): I WROTE THAT AT-660's COLLISION WAS THE HARMLESS ONE AND THAT IS WRONG. I compared `title` only, found the two AT-660 titles byte-equal at 622 chars with `status` the sole difference, and called it harmless while calling AT-661 dangerous. Their `evidence` fields differ: 3902 chars against 2520, and neither contains the other. So during the same minutes that AT-661 was ambiguous by title, AT-660 was ambiguous by EVIDENCE -- an id-keyed read returned one of two different evidence texts depending on line order. BOTH collisions were the dangerous class; AT-660 merely hid it in a field my comparison did not reach, which is C12's shape a third time in one day and is why the correction belongs in this row rather than in a message: the row is what the next session reads. The practical consequence is that the AT-676 guard case is STRONGER than this row originally argued, not weaker -- 2 of 2 merge collisions were content-divergent, not 1 of 2, and a title-only duplicate check would have reported the dangerous one as benign.
evidence: `qa/issues.jsonl` after the peer's commits: 707 rows, and an existing `AT-698` with `found_by: checker`, severity high, dated 2026-09-28, whose subject is the at570 unit (UI case runs refused with no way to create a live_case approval) -- i.e. written by the dispatched at570 checker, not by this seat. Highest numeric id = 698, so a naive next-free allocator in either checker returns the same number. This seat's append script asserts `id not in ids` before writing and aborted with `AssertionError: COLLISION: AT-698`, leaving the file untouched (the `&&` chain also prevented the commit, so nothing half-landed). Note the guard is a script-local convention in the checker's own append scripts, NOT a property of the ledger: `docs/FEATURES.jsonl` raises on duplicate ids at load and append (ledger/store.py), `qa/issues.jsonl` has `merge=union` and no guard at all (AT-676), so the same race in a session without the convention lands silently.
expected: Two separable things. (1) The reservation must be keyed to a HOLDER, not a role -- e.g. the standing seat takes AT-690..AT-699 and each dispatched checker is handed an explicit sub-range in its brief, or ids are allocated by the `reserve_id` kernel tool that qa/adapter.json already declares (`tools.reserve_id: kernel`) rather than by reading the ledger's frontier. The second is strictly better because it removes the frontier read that both allocators race on. (2) Until then, a working de-confliction, which is what this seat did rather than waiting: allocate from the TOP of the block downward (AT-709, AT-708, ...) because a sequential allocator takes from the bottom, so two allocators walking toward each other collide last instead of first. That is a mitigation, not a fix -- it fails when the block is nearly full -- and it is recorded so the next session does not mistake a descending id for an error. `qa/QUEUE.md` is the maker's surface; reported here, not edited. Filed medium: no duplicate was created, but the mechanism that prevented it was one script's convention, and AT-676's whole point is that a guard living in a convention is not a guard.
source: Found 2026-09-28 by the checker's own pre-append guard firing during the attempt to file AT-698 -- the collision was prevented rather than discovered afterwards, which is the first time today that happened in this ledger

title: The instruction that actually prevented a wrong finding today -- 'verify my framings rather than trusting them' -- exists only as ad-hoc text one maker happened to type into one dispatch. It is in no template, so it reaches a checker only when the dispatching session remembers it. On 2026-09-28 both seats made the same class of error within an hour (attributing a working-tree measurement to a commit), each caught it in the OTHER's message and neither in their own, and the thing that stopped a wrong finding being charged against a correct build was that one sentence. Nothing carried it to either of us, and nothing carries it to the next checker dispatched by a session that does not think of it. | REFINEMENT OF THIS ROW'S CLAIM ABOUT WHICH CONTROL TO BUILD, 2026-09-28, and it is a limit on something I wrote rather than a widening (the maker's, accepted). I had closed a report with 'five self-inflicted errors today were caught by the other seat or by a guard, and not one was caught by intending to be careful.' The observation is real; the sentence overreaches. At n=5, across two seats, on a single day when both were unusually error-prone AND unusually well-instrumented, it supports 'intending to be careful did not catch THESE FIVE.' It does not support 'intention never catches them', and the difference has a design consequence rather than being a quibble: the stronger version quietly argues that review is the only control worth building, which would be the wrong lesson from this day. THE THREE THINGS THAT ACTUALLY SAVED SOMETHING, named because they are heterogeneous and that is the finding: (1) a formatting diff run for an unrelated reason -- it caught the `.last-sweep` truncation (AT-699); (2) a DISPATCH INSTRUCTION, which is this row's own subject -- 'verify my framings rather than trusting them', which stopped a wrong finding being charged against a correct build; (3) the other seat reading a claim its author could not see was wrong -- five times, in both directions. Only (2) is a control anyone designed on purpose, and it is the one that exists in no template, which is precisely what this row asks for. So the evidence for this row is stronger than it was and the evidence for 'more review' is weaker than my sentence implied: a cheap instruction written once into a template out-performed both alertness and volume of review on the day it was measured.
evidence: The sequence is on the record across today's commits and both sessions' messages: the maker dispatched the at570 checker with its SNAPSHOT framing stated as an established contradiction; that brief happened to include an instruction to verify framings; the framing was then found wrong (a working-tree doctor result attributed to master) and the checker's own counter-evidence was wrong the same way (AT-662's tenth instance -- both legs read the working tree while claiming master; `git show 82677b26:docs/SNAPSHOT.md | grep -c F-065` -> 0 against 2 on disk). Both framings wrong, both caught, neither by its author. The defence that held was not either agent's alertness but a sentence in one dispatch. Checked what carries it structurally: the handshake's durable surfaces are the manifest, the verdict and the contract, and none has a field for what the checker was told about the maker's REASONING. The peer stated the limit itself and that statement is the finding: it worked 'because the checker was already dispatched with that instruction. Nothing carries it to a checker that has not been dispatched yet, and nothing carried it to either of us.'
expected: One line in the dispatch template rather than in anyone's recollection of having been careful once. Direction: a dispatch brief should state that any FRAMING it carries (a claimed contradiction, a 'this pre-exists on master', a 'behaviour-preserving' claim) is the maker's reasoning and not evidence, and must be re-derived before being relied on or charged. THE FIX PROBABLY LIVES OUTSIDE THIS BOUND ROOT -- the checker-dispatch template is in the global `maker` skill (~/.claude/skills/maker/SKILL.md), which this seat neither reads nor writes under its project binding -- so this is a proposal to Umesh, not a work item either session can take. The cheaper in-root half, if he prefers it: the same requirement stated once in qa/contracts/loop-status.md, which binds every checker working in this repo regardless of its dispatch text. I have NOT written that criterion, because a contract clause about dispatch practice is a scope call rather than a correction. Filed medium, not low: it is the only defence measured today that would have worked if BOTH sessions had been sloppy, and it is one forgotten sentence away from absent.
source: The peer's observation, 2026-09-28, stated as the limit of its own good outcome rather than as a virtue; filed by the checker because the ledger is where a structural gap survives the session that noticed it -- the same argument the row itself makes

title: `qa/.last-sweep` is an append-only sweep LOG -- 15 lines of history back to 2026-09-18, several of them the only record of what a sweep found and of corrections to earlier sweeps -- and nothing enforces the append. It is a plain file written by whatever the current checker reaches for, so a single `>` in place of `>>` destroys the entire history, silently and with no diff to read afterwards if it is committed in the same breath as real work. This seat did exactly that on 2026-09-28: `date -u ... > qa/.last-sweep` replaced all 15 lines with one, self-caught only because the next command was a format check against `git show HEAD:qa/.last-sweep`. Restored with `git checkout --`; nothing was lost. The analogous logs ARE protected -- `docs/DECISIONS.md` has a PreToolUse hook denying direct Edit/Write and a single `scripts/append_decision.ps1` write path, and `docs/FEATURES.jsonl` has `autotester ledger add` plus two id guards in ledger/store.py -- while the checker's own equivalent has neither a writer nor a guard.
evidence: `git show HEAD:qa/.last-sweep | wc -l` -> 15; after `date -u +... > qa/.last-sweep`, `wc -l` -> 1 and `git diff --stat` -> `1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 15 deletions(-)`. The destroyed lines included the 2026-09-27T22:42:35Z CORRECTION recording the AT-670 id collision and its cause, and the 2026-09-27T23:01:07Z FOLLOW-THROUGH recording AT-692's measurements -- both of which exist nowhere else in that form. Restored by `git checkout -- qa/.last-sweep` (15 lines back) and the new stamp appended with `>>` (16). Contrast, measured: `.claude/settings.json` wires a PreToolUse guard over docs/DECISIONS.md and the only documented write path is scripts/append_decision.ps1 (CLAUDE.md Lab Protocol); docs/FEATURES.jsonl is written only by `autotester ledger add` and raises on duplicate ids at load and append. `qa/.last-sweep` has no wrapper, no hook, and no schema -- its append-only-ness lives entirely in each checker noticing that the file already has content.
expected: One of two, both cheap, and the choice is not the checker's to make since either touches a surface it does not own. (a) A tiny writer -- `autotester sweep stamp "<line>"` alongside the existing `autotester ledger add` -- which appends, refuses an empty line, and is the only documented path; this is the FEATURES.jsonl pattern already in the repo and is preferable because it also gives the line a schema instead of free prose. title: `tests/test_flake_probe_real_process.py::test_run_once_kills_a_real_hung_process_and_its_real_grandchild` has no representation for 'my own scenario never started', so it reports that state as a failure of the behaviour it guards -- and UNDER LOAD IT CANNOT DETECT THE MUTATION IT WAS WRITTEN TO CATCH. Its docstring says it exists because an earlier sibling asserted only that run_once returned, and 'a mutation removing the tree kill survived it'. But its load failure mode is FileNotFoundError on `child.pid`, and a build with run_once's tree kill REMOVED ENTIRELY would produce the same FileNotFoundError on the same line under the same load, because the grandchild still never starts. The two are indistinguishable from the red. So the guard is unavailable exactly when the suite is loaded, and its absence looks identical to the load failure. This is the C12 shape inside the test the checker had been ready to excuse as a flake an hour earlier. | THE BOUND IS BELOW THE SCENARIO'S FLOOR COST, MEASURED 2026-09-28, which reclassifies this from load-sensitive to simply too small. The race is: nested pytest launch -> `test_hang` body executes `Popen` -> grandchild writes child.pid, all against the 10.0s timeout. Measured with the EXACT argv from scripts/flake_probe.py:170-173 (`sys.executable -m pytest <abs-nodeid> -q -p no:cacheprovider -o addopts=`), cwd = repo root because run_once's Popen passes no `cwd=` and so inherits it, PYTHONUTF8=1, running ONE NO-OP TEST and nothing else: 11.59s, 9.76s, 10.32s, 9.57s -- median 10.32s against a bound of 10.00s. pytest's own self-reported time for that no-op was `1 passed in 7.71s`, so ~2.6s more sits in interpreter and plugin bootstrap outside pytest's clock. The same argv from a cwd with no repo conftest in scope: 1.84s, 2.06s, 2.23s. So ~8s of the cost is this repo's own conftest and collection, and `addopts` is only `-q` (pyproject:66) so `-o addopts=` removes nothing expensive -- the number is not inflated by my instrument. CONSEQUENCE: the grandchild is spawned only in runs where startup happens to finish under 10s, which on a FREE machine is about a coin flip. That explains the observed pattern exactly -- 0 of 4 full-suite runs and 3 of 4 isolated runs -- without any nondeterminism in `run_once` at all. AND IT CHANGES THE FIX: a bounded poll for child.pid alone is NOT sufficient, because with the bound below the floor the poll would simply report 'scenario never started' most of the time. The fix needs BOTH halves -- (i) a bound that exceeds the scenario's measured floor with real margin (the floor is nested-pytest startup, ~10s here, not the 600s sleep), and (ii) the missing-file branch kept separate from the kill assertion so the two states can never look alike. (i) without (ii) leaves the conflation for a slower machine; (ii) without (i) converts a red into a permanent 'scenario never started' skip, which is silencing by another name. | FIXED AND CHECKER-VERIFIED, 2026-09-28, at700-setup-vs-subject cycle 2 (commit 9b142654, production half 2782083e). Reproduced by this seat on a clean extraction of the submitted commit: unmodified `2 passed in 24.72s`; `kill_tree(proc)` -> `proc.kill()` reddens at `tests/test_flake_probe_real_process.py:125` with `AssertionError: run_once killed pytest but left its real grandchild running`, `_alive(47636)` -- the line that never executed in cycle 1. The half no capability row claimed was falsified separately: with the tree kill INTACT and `BOUND_S = 1` so the grandchild cannot start, the red lands at `:119` as `Failed: scenario never started ... This says NOTHING about run_once's tree kill, passing or broken`, `1 failed in 2.69s`. Different line, different exception type, different message, and the setup branch explicitly disclaims the subject -- so the two arrangements this row exists to separate now produce readings that cannot be mistaken for one another, which is the criterion rather than the intention. Verdict: qa/verdicts/at700-setup-vs-subject.md.
evidence: Full-suite run on merged master, machine not idle: `1 failed, 2166 passed, 6 skipped, 14 xfailed in 1578.08s`. THE FAILING ASSERTION IS NOT THE KILL ASSERTION -- three passed first (`run.timed_out is True`, `run.returncode == flake_probe.TIMED_OUT`, `elapsed < 60`, the last with its own message 'the 10s bound must actually bound the call'), so run_once did time out and did return in bounds. Nested pytest startup alone can exceed 10s on a loaded machine. title: A capability-coverage row can be honestly produced and still be false of the artifact, because nothing binds the row to the commit it is submitted with. at700-setup-vs-subject cycle 1 reported its central falsification as reddening at the kill assertion; on the committed tree `6fd9dcaa` the same edit reddens on `PermissionError [WinError 32]` at `scripts/flake_probe.py:184` and never reaches that assertion. Both observations are real. They are observations of DIFFERENT TREES: the row was run against a working tree containing the AT-701 production fix, and that fix was never committed, while the manifest describes it in the past tense and the ledger marks AT-701 `fixed`. No fabrication and no carelessness in the measurement itself -- the gap is that a manifest records what a check DID and never records WHERE, so a state that no longer exists is reported as a property of one that does. | REFINED BY THE UNIT'S OWN AUTHOR, 2026-09-28, and the refinement is the load-bearing half. The maker -- the instance this row was filed against -- observed that HEAD-plus-porcelain-digest provenance catches ITS failure (a dirty tree) and not the inverse: a row run against a tree that is CLEAN but at the WRONG COMMIT, after a checkout or on a stale worktree, records a pristine digest and reads as impeccable provenance. It is right, and the consequence for the criterion is exact: **the criterion must be the COMPARISON, not the recording.** A recorded HEAD that nothing diffs against the submitted commit is a field, not a check -- the same shape as L9, where the guard sat on a surface that could not break. So when this lands it reads: the checker refuses any capability row whose recorded HEAD is not the submitted commit, and treats a non-empty porcelain digest as disclosure rather than disqualification. ALSO RECORDED, the cause, which no audit would have surfaced and which the maker volunteered: it ran `git checkout -- scripts/flake_probe.py` to undo the MUTATION after the falsification, and that reverted the still-uncommitted AT-701 fix in the same stroke because both lived in one file. The hygiene step destroyed the work; the manifest was then written from what had been watched rather than from what was on disk, and the ledger followed the manifest -- three artifacts agreeing with each other and none with the tree. That mechanism is an argument for the comparison form above and NOT for any rule against working dirty: AT-701 exists only because there was an uncommitted fix to try.
evidence: Checker-produced, 2026-09-28, in a throwaway copy of `git archive 6fd9dcaa` extracted outside the bound root, named test green in the copy first (`1 passed in 21.81s`). (a) Mutation only (`kill_tree(proc)` -> `proc.kill()`): `scripts lake_probe.py:184: in run_once / log.unlink(missing_ok=True) / E PermissionError: [WinError 32] ... flake-probe-36952-1.log`, `1 failed in 21.04s`, line 125 never executed. (b) Same mutation PLUS the AT-701 fix as the manifest describes it (best-effort unlink, failure into `notes`, run still returned): `E AssertionError: run_once killed pytest but left its real grandchild running / assert not True / where True = _alive(29064)` at `tests	est_flake_probe_real_process.py:125` -- exactly the manifest's row. So the row reproduces if and only if the uncommitted half is restored. Absence confirmed four ways: `git diff 77836e1b..6fd9dcaa --stat` (no `scripts/` path), `git log --oneline -3 -- scripts/flake_probe.py` (newest `0ed84a7a`, predating the unit), `git show 6fd9dcaa:scripts/flake_probe.py` line 184 (bare unlink), `git status --short` (only `.goal/`). Ledger read: `AT-701 medium status=fixed fixed_date=2026-09-28`.
expected: A capability row must name the tree it was run against, and that name must be checkable. Cheapest form that would have caught this with no new tooling: every row carries the `git rev-parse HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain` digest taken AT THE MOMENT the row was run, and the checker refuses any row whose recorded state does not match the submitted commit -- a dirty-tree digest is not disqualifying, it is disclosure, and it is the disclosure that was missing here. Stronger form, if it proves worth the cost: the falsification runs from a clean extraction of the submitted commit rather than from the author's working tree, which is what this seat already does on the checking side and what makes the asymmetry visible at all. NOT PROPOSED: forbidding uncommitted work while falsifying -- that is how the rows get found in the first place, and AT-701 itself was discovered BY running one. The defect is the missing binding, not the working tree. Filed high because the failure is silent and self-flattering in exactly one direction: a row run against a MORE complete tree than the one shipped always reports better behaviour than the artifact has, and every incentive points that way.

title: A fix can land, be checker-verified, and leave every open row that describes the old mechanism untouched -- and those rows keep being read, quoted and built on as current. AT-660/CN10 unified `0` to mean ZERO at both the gate and the run budget, and is `status: verified`. Three HIGH rows written AFTER it (AT-675, AT-683, AT-661) each rest on the pre-fix reading that `0` means UNBOUNDED. A human-facing gate (qa/gates/at674) was then assembled from those rows and put in front of Umesh for a decision, carrying the inverted claim that no UI-granted approval can ever BOUND probes -- when in current code every UI grant authorises ZERO probes and refuses every probing run. The direction of the reported risk was backwards in the artifact a human was deciding on.
evidence: Re-derived from source by the checker, not from any row. `core/consent.py::_shortfalls:56-59` compares `actions > approval.max_actions` plainly. `stages/run_budget.py::try_consume:64-71` does the same and returns False on `approval.wall_clock_s <= 0`; its docstring :36-41 states the change: 'every bound means the same thing here as it does at the gate, namely that ZERO GRANTS NOTHING. The truthiness guards this replaces (`if approval.max_actions and ...`) made 0 mean unlimited during the run while the gate read the same 0 as a zero budget.' `schema/approval.py:56-75` carries 'ZERO MEANS ZERO' on all three fields. `parallel_run.py:164` -- the line all three rows cite as holding the falsy guard -- is now `budget.try_consume(...)`. `grep -c max_probes src/autotester/ui/routes_crawl_approval.py` -> 0, so AT-675's underlying defect (no form field) is real while its stated consequence is inverted. Ledger: AT-660 `verified`; AT-675, AT-683, AT-661 all `open` and all dated after it.
expected: Not a request to edit the three rows -- they carry appended corrections now and their original text stands as history, which is L8's discipline. The structural ask is a BACK-REFERENCE at close-out: when a row moves to `fixed`/`verified`, the closing agent searches the open ledger for rows citing the same mechanism (the file:line it changed, or the invariant it inverted) and appends a pointer to each. Mechanisable cheaply, because the closing commit already knows which paths it touched: any open row whose `evidence` or `title` names a path the fix modified is a candidate, and the list is small enough to judge by hand. THE SHARPER POINT, and the reason this is high rather than medium: the failure did not stop at the ledger. A gate file was BUILT from the stale rows and shown to a human as the basis for a decision, so the defect propagated from an internal record into the one artifact whose whole job is to be correct for someone who cannot check it. Any close-out rule that stops at `qa/issues.jsonl` and does not reach `qa/gates/` is incomplete. Related but distinct from AT-710 (a cited id that does not resolve): here every citation resolves and the CONTENT is what went stale, which no resolver can catch.

title: AT-673's fix reads the LAST cycle field in a VERDICT as the current one, justified by LS6 -- but LS6 is a rule about MANIFESTS, and the two files order their history in OPPOSITE directions. A manifest appends each new cycle BELOW, so last-wins is correct there and at483 proves it. A verdict may keep the newer verdict ON TOP with the superseded one preserved beneath, which is what the checker skill's own concurrent-verdict rule produces. Measured over all 280 verdicts: 40 carry more than one cycle value, 39 of them ascend (last = highest, last-wins correct), and exactly ONE descends -- qa/verdicts/at700-setup-vs-subject.md, first=2 (## Cycle checked: 2, commit 9b142654), last=1 (## Cycle checked: 1, commit 6fd9dcaa, FAIL preserved). On that file the hook reads the cycle as 1.
evidence: Re-derived by this seat, not taken from the manifest: both cycle regexes implemented in Python over qa/manifests/*.md and qa/verdicts/*.md, comparing the FIRST match against the LAST per file. 40 verdicts disagree between first and last; 39 ascend; at700-setup-vs-subject.md is the single descending case, and it is the checker's own file, written under the rule that a superseded verdict is preserved rather than overwritten. THE DIRECTION IS FAIL-CLOSED, which is why this is not a FAIL of AT-673 (core-invariants C12): an under-read cycle makes `$vc -lt $mc` true, so the unit is added to `pending` and AUTO-CONTINUE stays ARMED. It over-reports work, never hides it. The cost is noise plus a second, subtler effect worth naming: a unit misread as pending can never be counted as an unclosed PASS, so one wrong read suppresses the very signal AT-673 was opened to fix.
expected: Read the cycle as the MAXIMUM of the fields present, not the last one. A cycle number only ever increases, both files agree on that, and max is correct under both orderings without needing either file to declare which line is authoritative -- so it is strictly weaker than an LS6-style declaration and needs no writer to change anything. Either way the falsifying test is available and cheap: a verdict holding `Cycle checked: 2` above `Cycle checked: 1`, with the manifest at Fix cycle 2, must report (0, 1) and not (1, 0).

title: `git commit --only -- <paths>` commits the WORKING-TREE state of those paths, not the change the author made. On commit ded3fbfc my ledger append of one row (AT-716) also carried FIVE rows of checker annotations I did not write and had not reviewed: checker_note filled on AT-674/AT-661/AT-675/AT-698/AT-683 (905-1295 chars each, all None in HEAD) and status open->wontfix on AT-661/AT-675/AT-698. Net effect was additive -- 722 -> 723 rows, no row lost, no field emptied -- so nothing was destroyed; the defect is that a commit message describing a verdict silently also enacted three issue closures.
evidence: Measured after the fact on my own commit, not suspected. `git status --porcelain` at HEAD=a30ff712, minutes before the append, listed qa/issues.jsonl as CLEAN (5 modified paths, none of them the ledger). The ledger's mtime at commit time is 18:00:41, which is my own append script's write. A field-by-field JSON diff of ded3fbfc^ against ded3fbfc shows the five rows above differing in checker_note and status, with the OLD value None/open in every case, and `ids only in OLD: []` -- so the annotations entered the working tree between the status call and the append, from a writer other than that script. The intervening commit 97f1fbe1 does not touch qa/issues.jsonl (its stat is two files: a gate and a manifest), so the source is an UNCOMMITTED write, not a merge. qa/verdicts/sweep-2026-09-28.md does not record these closures and predates them (mtime 04:26), so they do not belong to the last recorded sweep. WHICH writer produced them is NOT established and is not claimed here; the annotation text says 'this sweep' and 'TOP QUEUE ITEM this sweep', which is consistent with a checker sweep subagent whose ledger write was never committed -- the same work-exists-only-in-a-working-tree class as QA-1445 and AT-699.
expected: Two separable fixes. (1) Before a narrow-path ledger commit, diff the staged path against HEAD and confirm the change set matches the change the commit message claims -- `git diff --cached --stat` plus an id-level JSON diff for the ledger, since a one-row append that reports six changed rows is the signal. (2) A checker sweep that annotates the ledger must COMMIT its own ledger write in the same tick, for the same reason a verdict must be committed: an annotation that lives only in a working tree is one `git clean` from being lost, and until it is committed any other agent's narrow commit can adopt it. Not filed against the annotations themselves -- they are on the checker's own write surface and their content reads as genuine sweep output; they are left in place and are now committed, which is strictly better than where they were.
